约束就是查询Constraints Are Queries

谓词逻辑可以表达大量有意义的约束。前面介绍的每种机制都只能实现其中一个狭窄的子类：Predicate logic can express an enormous number of interesting constraints. Each of the mechanisms earlier can only implement a narrow subclass:

  • REFERENCES 只能实现 all s in S: (some t in T: s.col1 = t.col2)。REFERENCES only implements all s in S: (some t in T: s.col1 = t.col2).

  • UNIQUE 只能实现 all x, y in S: (x.col1 != y.col1) || (x.col2 != y.col2) ...UNIQUE only implements all x, y in S: (x.col1 != y.col1) || (x.col2 != y.col2) ...

  • CHECK 只能实现 all x in S: P(x)，其中 P 不使用任何量词。换句话说，CHECK 无法根据其他行来约束某一行。CHECK only implements all x in S: P(x), where P does not use any quantifiers. In other words, CHECK cannot constrain a row based on other rows.

那么，“所有书籍的作者都出生于出版日期之前”这样的要求，该如何实现呢？用逻辑很容易表达：How would we implement something like “all books have an author born before the publication date”? It is easy to express logically:

constraint NoTimeTravel =
  all b in books:
    some a in authors:
      1. b.author_id = a.id
      2. b.published_on > a.birthday

实现 NoTimeTravel 就是另一回事了。用 REFERENCES 不行（因为它有两个条件），用 CHECK 也不行（因为它使用了第二个量词），用 UNIQUE 更不行（原因很明显）。那么，数据库能强制实施这个约束吗？还是说我们只能在应用端进行验证？Implementing NoTimeTravel is another matter. It cannot be done with REFERENCES (as it has two conditions), nor with CHECK (as it uses a second quantifier), nor with UNIQUE (obvious). So can our databases enforce this, or are we limited to application-side validation?

事实证明，大多数 SQL 数据库确实能强制实施这个约束！我们只需花一点功夫，运用一些逻辑规则就能做到。首先，可以把 NoTimeTravel 拆分为一个“简单”约束和一个“困难”约束：It turns out most SQL databases, can, in fact, enforce this constraint! We just have to put in a little work and apply some logical rules to get there. First, we can split NoTimeTravel into an “easy” constraint and a “hard” constraint:

# Just a foreign key
constraint BooksAuthorsFK =
  all b in books:
    some a in authors:
      b.author_id = a.id

constraint NoTimeTravel =
  all b in books:
    all a in authors:
      b.author_id != a.id ||
        b.published_on > a.birthday

我们把 NoTimeTravel 中的 some 改成了 all，还把主体改成了“要么作者不同，要么书籍出版于作者出生之后”。虽然也可以使用 =>，但 SQL 没有蕴含运算符，所以写成 !P || Q 更贴近最终的实现。再结合 BooksAuthorsFK 强制每本书恰好有一位作者，这就与原来的约束等价。下一步并非严格必需，但能让最终结果更清楚：We turned the some in NoTimeTravel into an all. We also changed the body to be “either the author is different or the book was published after the author was born”. While we could have used a => instead, SQL does not have an implication operator, so writing !P || Q keeps us closer to the eventual implementation. This, combined with BooksAuthorsFK forcing each book to have exactly one author, is equivalent to our original constraint. Our next step is not strictly necessary, but will clarify our final outcome:

constraint NoTimeTravel =
  all (b, a) in books x authors:
      b.author_id != a.id ||
        b.published_on > a.birthday

现在来看关键洞见。如果这个约束不成立，就必定存在某个违反它的具体反例 (book, author)。而我们可以编写一个查询来找出这个反例！如果查询没有结果，就知道不存在反例，也就意味着约束成立。这不过是逻辑对偶性的又一个例子！Now for the insight. If this constraint does not hold, there must be a specific (book, author) counterexample that violates it. And we can write a query to find the counterexample! If the query turns up nothing we know there are no counterexamples, meaning the constraint holds. This is just another example of logical duality!

constraint NoTimeTravel =
  !some (b, a) in books x authors:
      !(b.author_id != a.id ||
        b.published_on > a.birthday)

# Apply De Morgan's Law
constraint NoTimeTravel =
  !some (b, a) in books x authors:
      1. b.author_id = a.id
      2. b.published_on <= a.birthday

这可以直接对应到一个 SQL 查询：This directly maps to a SQL query:

-- NoTimeTravel holds if this finds 0 rows

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books as b
   INNER JOIN authors as a
   ON b.author_id = a.id
   AND b.published_on <= a.birthday;

要真正强制实施这个约束，可以使用 SQL“触发器”，即设置为在行或表发生变更时运行的存储过程。我们只需声明一个触发器，执行这个查询，并在查询结果非空时抛出异常。为简洁起见，示例另附于代码示例 [https://github.com/logicforprogrammers/book-assets]中。To actually enforce the constraint, we can use a SQL “trigger”, or a stored procedure set to run on row or table changes. All we need to do is declare a trigger trigger that makes this query and raises an exception if the query is nonempty. For brevity, an example is separately provided with the code samples [https://github.com/logicforprogrammers/book-assets].

状态变更约束State Change Constraints

SQL 触发器还有一个有用的特性：由记录更新触发时，它们可以检查有关记录如何变更的约束。例如，我们可以强制 updated_at 时间戳只能向未来推进，或者当一个可空字段具有非 NULL 值后，就不能再设回 NULL。SQL triggers have one other useful feature: when triggered by a record update, they can check constraints on how the record changed. We can for example enforce that an updated_at timestamp can only go forwards in time or that when a nullable field has a non-NULL value, it cannot be set back to NULL.

在前面的章节里，我们已经表示过变更：在变更断言中，我们使用了 old(x) 和 x；而在 决策表中，我们使用了 x 和 x'（读作“x 撇”）。SQL 语法使用 NEW 和 OLD，但为了让后面的一章更容易理解，我现在就使用带撇号的语法。We have already represented changes in previous chapters: in change assertions we used old(x) and x, while in decision tables we used x and x' (“x prime”). SQL syntax uses NEW and OLD, but to make a later chapter easier I will use the prime syntax right now.

constraint NoNullAfterAdmin =
  all g in Groups:
    g.admin_id != NULL => g.admin_id' != NULL

一旦 admin_id 不为 null，它的下一个值也不能是 null，这意味着它再也不能变回 null。Once the admin_id is not null, the next value cannot be null either, meaning that it can never go back to null.

这也适用于状态机列：一条记录可以经历 WAITING -> READY 或 READY -> DONE，但不能经历 WAITING -> DONE。这种情况下，通常应该“允许 x 变成它自身”：This is also useful for state machine columns: a record can go WAITING -> READY or READY -> DONE, but not WAITING -> DONE. In that case it’s considered good form to “allow x to change to itself”:

constraint StateMachineTransitions ==
  all t in tasks:
    1. t.status = "WAITING" => t.status' in {"WAITING", "READY"}
    2. t.status = "READY => t.status' in {"READY", "DONE"}

练习：转移辅助谓词Exercise: Transition Helper

编写一个辅助谓词 ValidTransitions(task, from, to)，使我们能够这样写出 StateMachineTransitions 的主体：Write a helper predicate ValidTransitions(task, from, to), so that we can write the body of StateMachineTransitions this way:

all t in tasks:
  1. ValidTransitions(task, "WAITING", {"READY"})
  2. ValidTransitions(task, "READY", {"DONE"})

注意，to 将是一个转移的集合。Note that to is going to be a set of transitions.

解答Solution

小结Summary

  1. 数据库是表的集合，而表是记录的集合。Databases are sets of tables, which are sets of records.

  2. some 量词对应数据库查询。联接是对两个或更多表的笛卡尔积进行的查询。对于 SQL，大多数 some 表达式都能直接翻译为查询，不过可能需要把抽象谓词内联展开。The some quantifiers corresponds to database queries. Joins are queries over the Cartesian product of two or more tables. In the case of SQL, most some expressions are directly translatable to queries, though you may need to inline abstract predicates.

  3. all 表达式对应数据库约束，all-some 嵌套表达式对应外键。数据库有不同的功能来强制实施约束。约束既可以针对数据，也可以针对数据的变更方式。all expressions correspond to database constraints, and all-some nested expressions correspond to foreign keys. Databases have different features for enforcing constraints. Constraints may be on data, or how data changes.

  4. 利用对偶性，我们可以通过查询约束的否定来检查约束。SQL 数据库可以借此通过触发器强制实施复杂约束。By using duality, we can check a constraint by querying its negation. SQL databases can use this to enforce complex constraints, via triggers.

到目前为止，我们的逻辑始终紧贴数据库：我们讨论的是数据库表和记录的性质。[[但数据库只是数据模型的一种不完美实现，而数据模型是我们试图使之清晰可理解的那部分世界的概念化表示。]] 下一章，我们将上升一个抽象层次，用逻辑研究数据模型。So far we’ve been keeping the logic very close to the database: we’re talking about properties of database tables and records. [[But the database is just an imperfect implementation of the data model, the conceptual slice of the world we’re trying to make legible.]] Next chapter we will use logic to study our data model, one level of abstraction higher.

延伸阅读Further Reading

本章的数据库表示法来自 Edgar Codd 的关系模型。关系模型最早在《大型共享数据库的数据关系模型》 [https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/362384.362685]中提出，同文还提出了一组构成关系代数的运算符。这里 [https://cs186berkeley.net/notes/note6/]有一篇更平易近人的关系代数介绍。SQL 以关系代数为基础，但并未完全遵循它。The database representation in this chapter comes from Edgar Codd’s Relational Model. The relational model was first introduced in A relational model of data for large shared data banks [https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/362384.362685], along with a set of operators that made the Relational Algebra. A gentler introduction to relational algebra can be found here [https://cs186berkeley.net/notes/note6/]. SQL is based on relational algebra but does not follow it in its entirely.

了解数据库不变式所能实现的功能，最好的方式是阅读数据库的官方文档。虽然本章内容与 SQLite 兼容，但文档最完善的可以说是 Postgres：The best way to learn about the capabilities of database invariants is to read the official database documentation. While this chapter is compatible with SQLite, the best documented is arguably Postgres:

  • CHECK 约束 [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html]CHECK constraints [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html]

  • 触发器约束 [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createtrigger.html]Trigger constraints [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createtrigger.html]

数据建模Data Modeling

注Note

本章计划重写；数据库一章已在 v0.11 中重写，因此本章也需要更新。This is scheduled for a rewrite and needs to be updated after the databases chapter was rewritten in v0.11

上一章，我们用逻辑分析了数据库约束。为此，我们始终紧贴数据库语义：外键是数值列，实体之间的关系通过多对多关联表来建立，等等。In the last chapter, we used logic to figure out database constraints. To do so, we stuck close to database semantics: foreign keys are number columns, relationships between entities go through a many-to-many table, etc.

任何数据库模式都只是抽象数据模型的一种可能表示。在本章中，我们将用逻辑直接分析模型。Any database schema is only one possible representation of the abstract data model. In this chapter, we will use logic to analyze the model directly.

从数据中抽象Abstracting from Data

让我们取出上一章的记录：Let’s pull our records from the last chapter:

record Users {
  id: Int
}

record Groups {
  id: Int
  admin_id: Int
}

record GroupMembership {
  id: int
  user_id: int
  group_id: int
}

我看到了三个与抽象模型无关的“实现细节”：I see three “implementation details” that don’t matter to the abstract model:

  1. 我不在乎群组 id 是整数、UUID 还是别的什么，我真正关心的是各个群组彼此不同。I don’t care whether the group id is an integer or a UUID or something else, what I really care about is that the groups are distinct.

  2. 为什么 admin_id 是整数？为什么不能直接说 admin 是一个用户？数据库需要一个整数列，但在我们的脑海中，群组有的是管理员，而不是整数。Why is admin_id an integer? Why can’t we just say the admin is a user? The database needs an integer column, but in our heads, groups have admins, not integers.

  3. 说到这里，我们为什么需要 GroupMembership 记录？我们实际想表达的是，群组的成员是用户。或者说，用户属于群组。多对多关联表同样只是为了适应数据库而采用的实现细节。For that matter, why do we need a GroupMembership record? What we actually intend is that groups have members that are users. Or maybe that users belong to groups. The many-to-many table is, once again, just an implementation detail to work within the database.

这些东西都妨碍我们思考真正的数据模型。把它们全都丢开，只关注用户、群组及其关系，会更容易。This all gets in the way of thinking about the actual data model. It’d be easier to throw these all away and just focus on the users, the groups, and their relationships.

大致像这样：Something like this:

sig User {}

sig Group {
  admin: User
  members: set User
}

我用“sig”表示签名（signature），因为这些不是记录。它们只是数据模型，其中群组具有管理员和用户集合。没有任何实现细节渗入我的模型！I’m using “sig” for signature, because these are not records. They’re just a data model, where groups have admins and sets of users. No implementation details have leaked into my model!

（不过，即使这样也有一点倾向性：如果我们反而想让 member_of 成为 User 而非群组的一个元素呢？）(Though even this is biasing things a little: what if we instead wanted to have member_of be an element of the User and not the group?)

上一章的一个约束——群组管理员必须也是群组成员——很容易这样表达：One of the constraints from last chapter, that a group’s admin must also be a group member, is easily expressed like this:

all g in Group:
  g.admin in g.members

实践：形式化规约In Practice: Formal Specification

我先问两个问题：Let me start by asking two questions:

  1. 一个群组是否可能把系统中的每位管理员都包含为成员？Is it possible for one group to have every admin in the system as members?

  2. 一个群组是否可能没有成员？Is it possible for one group to have no members?

这些问题不算太复杂，你大概花几分钟就能推理出答案。但随着数据模型变得复杂，约束越来越精细，要在脑海中解决这些问题就愈发困难。这时，我们就希望让计算机替我们检查模型。These aren’t too complicated, and you can probably reason through them in a couple of minutes. But as the complexity of a data model grows, and we add increasingly elaborate constraints, it becomes progressively more difficult to solve these in your head. This is a place where we want the computer to check our model for us.

这正是形式化规约的领域：建立数据（或系统）的模型，并用工具检查其正确性。它是我们在前面一章首次介绍的形式化方法的另一面，只不过检查的是设计，而不是代码。And this is the domain of Formal Specification: creating models of data (or systems) and using tools to check them for correctness. It’s the other side of the formal methods coin that we first introduces in an earlier chapter, just checking designs instead of code.

形式化规约语言有很多种，不过我现在想用的是 Alloy [https://alloytools.org/]。我不会过多介绍 Alloy 的具体细节，那超出了本书的范围。但我会展示它如何解决这些问题。There are many different formal specification languages, but the one I want to use now is called Alloy [https://alloytools.org/]. I’m not going to go into too many of the specifics of Alloy; that’s beyond the scope of this book. But I’ll show you how it solves these problems.

首先，我们定义数据模型的组成部分及约束：First, we define the components of our data model and our constraints:

sig User {}

sig Group {
  admin: User,
  members: set User
}

pred admins_members_of_groups {
  all g: Group |
    g.admin in g.members
}

pred is_admin[u: User] {
  some g: Group |
    g.admin = u
}

注意，Alloy 的量词语法不同：它用 all g: Group | prop，而不是 all g in Group: prop。Note that Alloy uses a different syntax for quantifiers: all g: Group | prop instead of all g in Group: prop.

有了这些基础，我们就可以编写一个“命令”，让 Alloy 寻找满足某些性质的系统实例。在这里，让它寻找包含所有管理员的群组实例：Once we have the basics, we can write a “command”, telling Alloy to find examples of systems where certain properties are true. In this case, ask it for examples of groups containing all admins:

run group_with_all_admins {
  admins_members_of_groups &&
  some g: Group |
    all u: User |
      is_admin[u] => u in g.members
}

运行 Alloy 内置的分析器（我使用 VSCode），就能得到实例的可视化图：Running Alloy’s built-in analyzer (I use VSCode) gives us a visualization of the example:

Alloy 还可以生成新的实例供可视化查看、更换主题，甚至针对特定实例运行 REPL。它是发现意外情况的绝佳工具！Alloy can also generate new examples to visualize, change the theme, and even run a REPL on specific examples. It’s a great tool for finding unexpected situations!

我们也可以让 Alloy 检查某个性质是否始终成立。这通常用来检查我们是否保证了某个数据不变式。例如，我们可能希望一个数据不变式是“群组永远非空”。We can also ask Alloy to check that a property always holds. This is usually used to check that we guarantee a data invariant. For example, we might want a data invariant to be “groups are never empty”.

check no_empty_groups {
  admins_members_of_groups =>
    all g: Group | some g.members
}

对此运行分析器，如果能找到反例，它就会给出反例的可视化图。不过在这里，它什么也没找到，因此我们可以更有信心地认为该性质成立。Running the analyzer on this would give us a visualization of a counterexample, if it can find one. In this case, though, it doesn’t find anything, so we can be more confident the property holds.

Executing "Check no_empty_groups"
No counterexample found. Assertion may be valid. 2ms.

抽象Abstractions

规约语言处于比编程语言更高的抽象层次，这意味着它们能够表达并检查某些性质，而把这些性质编成程序来处理，在计算上可能很难行得通。让我们在数据模型中加入一条：某些用户可以有另一位用户作为其推荐人。这很容易表示为数据库记录。Specification languages live at a higher level of abstraction that programming languages, meaning they can express and check properties that would be too computationally infeasible to program. Let’s add into our data model that some users can have another user who referred them. That’s easy to express as a database record.

record Users {
  id: Int
+ referrer: Int + NULL
}

这带来了一个新的数据不变式：用户不能是自己的推荐人。作为 SQL 约束，它大致会是 u.referrer != u.id。在 Alloy 中则是这样：This implies a new data invariant: users cannot be their own referrer. As a SQL constraint, it would look something like u.referrer != u.id. In Alloy, it would look like this:

sig User {
  referrer: lone User // 0 or 1
}

pred no_self_loops {
  all u: User |
    u != u.referrer
}

现在，再给这个约束加一点变化：任何用户都不能通过传递关系成为自己的推荐人。如果 Alice 推荐了 Bob，Bob 推荐了 Eve，那么 Eve 就不能曾经推荐过 Alice。Now, one more twist to the constraint: no user can transitively be their own referrer. If Alice refers Bob and Bob refers Eve, Eve cannot have referred Alice.

这在 SQL 中极其困难。至少需要使用递归公用表表达式，而得到的查询既复杂，计算开销也很大。This is extraordinary difficult in SQL. At the very least we’d need use recursive common table expressions, and the resulting query will be convoluted and computationally expensive.

另一方面，传递查询在 Alloy 中轻而易举。在 Alloy 中，Alice.^referrer 是推荐关系的“传递闭包”：一个包含 Alice 的推荐人、推荐人的推荐人、推荐人的推荐人的推荐人，等等的集合。On the other hand, transitive lookups are trivial in Alloy. In Alloy, Alice.^referrer is the “transitive closure” of referrals: the set containing Alice’s ref, the ref’s ref, the ref’s ref’s ref, etc.

同一个约束在 Alloy 中写作：The same constraint in Alloy:

pred no_cycles {
  all u: User |
    !(u in u.^referrer)
}

与实现and Implementations

能在 Alloy 中表达这个约束固然很好，但对实际的 SQL 数据库并没有帮助。SQL 仍然无法简洁地支持传递查询。It’s good that we can express the constraint in Alloy, but that doesn’t help us with our actual SQL database. SQL still doesn’t cleanly support transitive lookups.

不过，我们可以用 Alloy 找出一个能在 SQL 中实现、而且同样能保证 no_cycles 的约束。然后我们就测试But we can use Alloy to figure out an implementable SQL constraint that also guarantees no_cycles. Then we’d test

check { implementable_property => no_cycles }

这种情况下，我们会说 implementable_property 比 no_cycles 更强。我的一个想法是给用户规定某种顺序，比如按 id 或注册日期排序。这样，我猜想，如果我们只能推荐注册日期更早的人，就不会出现环。这在 SQL 中比较容易检查。In this case we’d say that implementable_property is stronger than no_cycles. One idea I have would be to place some ordering on users, like id or signup date. Then I’d predict that if we could only refer someone with an earlier signup date, we wouldn’t have any cycles. This would be relatively easy to check in SQL.

练习Exercise

用我们的记法（而不是 Alloy 的记法）写出约束：“如果用户有推荐人，那么该用户的 created_at 晚于推荐人的 created_at。”Write the constraint (in our notation, not Alloy’s) “If a user has a referrer, the user’s created_at is later than the referrers created_at.

解答Solution

在 Alloy 中：In Alloy:

sig User {
  referrer: lone User,
  created_at: disj Int
}

pred referral_must_come_later {
  all u, ref: User |
    u.referrer = ref => gt[u.created_at, ref.created_at]
}

现在可以检查，这个可实现的约束是否保证了数据模型的性质：Now we can check that our implementable constraint guarantees our data model property:

check implementation_works {
  referral_must_come_later => no_cycles
}

Alloy 检查通过，没有找到反例，因此我们可以有信心地认为这个约束达到了预期效果。Alloy 帮助我们找到了以低廉代价强制实施高成本数据模型约束的方法。Alloy passes this with no counterexample, so we can be confident this constraint does what we want. Alloy helped us find a cheap way of enforcing an expensive data model constraint.

“表明一个实现符合更抽象的模型”的技术术语是精化。The technical term for “showing an implementation matches a more abstract model” is refinement.

用规约寻找缺陷Finding Bugs with Specifications

形式化规约的主要用途是发现设计错误。设计错误比代码错误代价更高，因此更需要尽早发现。[[由于形式化规约处于更高的抽象层次，它们能更容易地发现设计错误。]]The main use-case of formal specifications is to find errors in designs. Design errors are more expensive than code errors, and so are more important to detect early. [[Since formal specifications live at a higher level of abstraction, they can more easily find design errors.]]

我教授 Alloy 时，会用一个简化的访问权限模型演示这一点。我们有一组 User 和 Resource。Resource 只能由其 readable_by 集合中的 User 读取。When I teach Alloy, I demonstrate this with a simplified model of access permissions. We have a set of Users and Resources. Resources can only be read by Users in their readable_by set.

sig User {}

sig Resource {
  readable_by: set User
}

pred can_access[u: User, r: Resource] {
  u in r.readable_by
}

run {some u: User, r: Resource | can_access[u, r]}

在此基础上，我们再规定某些资源具有父资源。如果资源是文件，父资源可以是它所在的文件夹。与前面的推荐关系示例一样，任何资源都不能通过传递关系成为自己的父资源。On top of this, we add that some resources have parents. If our resources are files, the parent could be the containing folder. As with our prior example of referrals, no resource can transitively be its own parent.

sig Resource {
  readable_by: set User
+ ,parent: lone Resource
}
+ fact no_cycles {
+ no r: Resource |
+   r in r.^parent
+}

最后，我们修改访问规则，使用户只要有权读取某个资源的父资源，就能访问该资源。Finally, we amend the access rule, so that a user can access a resource if they have permission to read its parent.

pred can_access[u: User, r: Resource] {
  u in r.readable_by
+ || u in r.parent.readable_by
}

加上这一条后，我问学员：“如果我们能访问某个资源，是否就保证能访问它的所有子资源？”After adding this, I ask my class “if we can access a resource, are we guaranteed to access all of its children?”

assert parent_implies_child {
  all u: User, r: Resource |
    can_access[u, r] =>
      all child: r.~parent | //r.~parent is `children of r`
        can_access[u, child]
}

check parent_implies_child

多数人惊讶地发现，答案是不，这个性质并不成立！和之前一样，我们可以用图的可视化形式查看反例，也可以将其输出为 ASCII 表格：Most people are surprised to find out no, this property does not hold! As before, we can see the counterexample as a graph visualizatin, but we can also output it as an ASCII table:

┌─────────────┬───────────┬──────────┐
│this/Resource│readable_by│parent    │
├─────────────┼───────────┼──────────┤
│Resource$0   │User$0     │          │
├─────────────┼───────────┼──────────┤
│Resource$1   │           │Resource$0│
├─────────────┼───────────┼──────────┤
│Resource$2   │           │Resource$1│
└─────────────┴───────────┴──────────┘

为了解释这个出错的实例，问题如下：To explain the error instance, this is the problem:

  1. 开始时有三个资源：Parent（Resource$0）、Child（Resource$1）和 Grandchild（Resource$2）。只有 Parent 的 readable_by 中包含这个 User。We start with three resources: Parent (Resource$0), Child (Resource$1), and Grandchild (Resource$2). Only Parent has the User in readable_by.

  2. 因为 User 可以访问 Parent，所以该性质断言它可以访问 Child。Because the User can access Parent, the property asserts they can access Child.

  3. 检查 Child 时，我们发现 User in Parent.readable_by，所以可以访问它。In checking Child, we see that User in Parent.readable_by, so we can access it.

  4. 因为我们可以访问 Child，所以该性质断言我们可以访问 Grandchild。Because we have access to Child, the property asserts we can access Grandchild.

  5. 这个 User 既不在 Child 的 readable_by 中，也不在 Grandchild 的该集合中。因此，我们无法访问 Grandchild。The User is not in Child or Grandchild’s readable_by. So we cannot access Grandchild.

  6. 我们可以访问 Child，却不能访问它的所有子资源，因此违反了该性质。We can access Child but not all of its children, leading to a property violation.

这才是形式化规约的真正威力：完整规约不到 30 行，却能发现许多经验丰富的开发者都会漏掉的细微错误。为修复它，我们可以修改 readable_by，通过传递关系检查一个资源的全部祖先。This is the real power of formal specification: the full spec is less than 30 lines and still finds a subtle error many experienced developers miss. To fix this, we can modify readable_by to transitively check a resource’s entire ancestry.

pred can_access[u: User, r: Resource] {
  u in r.readable_by
- || u in r.parent.readable_by
+ || u in r.^parent.readable_by
}

（和之前一样，我们仍然需要设法在数据库中实现传递约束。但着手实现一个正确的设计，总好过实现一个可能有问题的设计。）(As before, we would still need to find a way to implement a transitive constraint in our database. But it is always better to be working on implementing a correct design than to implement a possibly-broken one.)

小结Summary

  1. 我们可以在比数据库实现更高的抽象层次上表示数据（或其他系统）。We can represent data (or other systems) at a higher level of abstraction than what the database implements.

  2. 这样，我们就能用形式化规约语言直接测试这些抽象。By doing this, we can test the abstractions directly, in a formal specification language.

  3. Alloy 就是一种这样的形式化规约语言，能够生成满足性质的实例的可视化图。它还可以测试性质是否成立。Alloy is one such formal specification language, and can produce visualizations of satisfying properties. It can also test that properties hold.

  4. 因为处于更高的抽象层次，我们可以表达那些无法直接在数据库层面强制实施的不变式。Because we’re at a higher level of abstraction, we can express invariants that would be impossible to directly enforce at the database level.

  5. Alloy 可以测试某个可实现的约束是否也保证了抽象不变式。Alloy can test if an implementable constraint also guarantees an abstract invariant.

虽然数据建模是形式化规约的一个良好用例，但它在并发系统建模中才真正大放异彩。下一章，我们将展示形式化规约如何发现软件设计中的竞态条件。While data modeling is a good use case for formal specification, it really shines for modeling concurrent systems. In the next chapter, we will show how a formal specification can find race conditions in a software design.

系统建模System Modeling

上一章，我们展示了如何用形式化规约分析数据模型并寻找问题。但这只是规约这座冰山的一角。我们还可以用它为系统建模。In the last chapter, we showed how formal specification can be used to analyze a data model and look for problems. But that’s only the tip of the specification iceberg. We can also use it to model systems.

场景Situation

我们有一些银行用户。银行用户可以相互汇款。系统有透支保护，因此汇款不能让账户余额降到零以下。这很容易保证，只要在每笔汇款中加上一个 if 检查就行了！We have some bank users. Bank users can wire money to each other. We have overdraft protection, so wires cannot reduce an account value below zero. That’s easy to guarantee, just throw an if check on each wire and you’re done!

……但如果用户可以同时发起多笔汇款呢？如果计算机在处理一笔汇款的中途崩溃呢？如果有人试图给自己汇款呢？如果有人同时分多笔给自己汇款，随后某台服务器又崩溃了呢？…But what if users can send multiple wires at the same time? What if a computer crashes in the middle of processing a wire? What if someone tries to send themselves money? What if someone tries to send themselves money in multiple wires at the same time, and then one of the servers crash?

这就是我们需要为系统建模的原因。我们想确认，性质在每一种可能的行为下都成立，而不仅仅是在理想流程中成立。This is why we need to model systems. We want to see that our properties hold under every possible behavior, not just on the happy path.

我们将用逻辑来建模。And we’ll use logic to model it.

所用逻辑The Logic

我们将分三个阶段处理这个系统。首先，看看普通的谓词逻辑如何就足以准确地为问题建模。然后，对逻辑做一个简单扩展，以更优雅地表达规约。最后，将其翻译为一种真正的工具能够使用的形式，让工具直接检查我们的逻辑是否有错。We’re going to handle this system in three stages. First, we’ll see how our regular predicate logic is enough to accurately model our problem. Then, we’ll make a simple extension to our logic to more elegantly express the spec. Finally, we’ll translate it to a real tool that can directly check our logic for errors.

暂时假设系统极其简单：有两个硬编码的变量 alice 和 bob，初始时各有 10 美元，而且只允许从 Alice 向 Bob 转账。此外，转账完全是原子的：检查余额是否充足、取款和存款都发生在同一个瞬间。最终建模的系统会更复杂，这里只是为了说明这些思想。For now we’ll assume an extremely simple system: two hardcoded variables alice and bob, both start with 10 dollars, and transfers are only from Alice to Bob. Also, the transfer is totally atomic: we check for adequate funds, withdraw, and deposit all in a single moment of time. Our modeled system will be more complex; this is just to relate the ideas.

首先，来看系统的一个有效行为，也就是系统可能的一种演变方式。First, let’s look at a valid behavior of the system, or possible way it can evolve.

alice:  10 -> 5  -> 3  -> 3  -> ...
bob:    10 -> 15 -> 17 -> 17 -> ...

在编程中，我们会把 alice 和 bob 看作不断变化的变量。怎样才能纯粹用谓词逻辑表达这些变量？一种方式是用值的数组来替换它们。alice[0] 是 alice 的初始状态，alice[1] 是第一个时间步之后的状态，依此类推。于是，时间“不过”就是自然数集合。In programming, we’d think of alice and bob as variables that change. How can we express those variables purely in terms of predicate logic? One way would be to replace them with arrays of values. alice[0] is the initial state of alice, alice[1] is after the first time step, etc. Time, then, is “just” the set of natural numbers.

Time  = {0,  1,  2,  3, ...}
alice = [10, 5,  3,  3, ...]
bob   = [10, 15, 17, 17, ...]

那是一个有效行为。下面是一些无效行为：That is a valid behavior. Here are some invalid behaviors:

alice = [10, 3,  ...]
bob   = [10  15, ...]

alice = [10, -1,  ...]
bob   = [10  21,  ...]

第一个行为无效，是因为 Bob 收到的钱比 Alice 减少的钱多。第二个无效，是因为它违反了我们提出的不变式：账户余额不能为负。我们能否写出一个谓词，使其对有效转移为真，而对这两个无效行为中的某个转移为假？The first is invalid because Bob received more money than Alice lost. The second is invalid because it violates our proposed invariant, that accounts cannot go negative. Can we write a predicate that is true for valid transitions and false for some transition in our two invalid behaviors?

这是一种写法：Here’s one way:

Time = Nat

Transfer(t: Time) =
  some value in 0..=alice[t]:
    1. alice[t+1] == alice[t] - value
    2. bob[t+1] == bob[t] + value

逐一检查：对于有效行为中的每个 t，它都为真；对于无效行为中的至少一个 t，它为假。注意，Alice 没有发起转账的那些步骤也满足 Transfer，我们只需选择 value = 0。Go through and check that this is true for every t in the valid behavior and false for at least one t in the invalid behavior. Note that the steps where Alice doesn’t send a transfer also pass Transfer; we just pick value = 0.

现在，我可以写出一个谓词，完整描述什么是“有效行为”：I can now write a predicate that perfectly describes what a “valid behavior” is:

Spec =
  1. alice[0] == 10
  2. bob[0]   == 10
  3. all t in Time:
    Transfer(t)

不过，把“什么都没发生”当作“Alice 发起了一笔空转账”有点奇怪。在真实系统中，我们大概不希望人们不停地互相转账零美元：Now allowing “nothing happens” as “Alice sends an empty transfer” is a little bit weird. In the real system, we probably don’t want people to constantly be sending each other zero dollars:

Transfer(t: Time) =
- some value in 0..=alice[t]:
+ some value in 1..=alice[t]:
    1. alice[t+1] == alice[t] - value
    2. bob[t+1] == bob[t] + value

但这样一来，就不能有任何什么都没发生的时间步了。这意味着没有任何行为是有效的！But now there can’t be a timestep where nothing happens. And that means no behavior is valid!

练习：没有有效行为Exercise: No valid behaviors

解释为什么当前版本的规约不可能有任何有效行为，也就是说，至少对某些 t，Transfer(t) 为假。Explain why the current version of the spec cannot have any valid behaviors, ie for at least some t, Transfer(t) is false.

提示：记住，Time 是自然数的别名，这意味着每个行为都有无限多个步骤。Hint: Remember, Time is an alias for the natural numbers, meaning every behavior has an infinite number of steps.

解答Solution

因此，建模时通常会加入一个停顿步，如下所示：So typically when modeling we add a stutter step, like this:

Spec =
  1. alice[0] == 10
  2. bob[0]   == 10
  3. all t in Time:
    || Transfer(t)
    || 1. alice[t+1] == alice[t]
       2. bob[t+1] == bob[t]

（这也是我们能用无限行为对有限算法建模的原因。如果算法在 t=21 时完成，那么 t=22,23,24... 就全都是停顿步。）(This is also why we can use infinite behaviors to model a finite algorithm. If the algorithm completes at t=21, t=22,23,24... are all stutter steps.)

这里牵涉的部分已经够多了，我想把它拆成几个子谓词。There’s enough moving parts here that I’d want to break it into subpredicates.

Init =
  1. alice[0] == 10
  2. bob[0]   == 10

Stutter(t) =
  1. alice[t+1] == alice[t]
  2. bob[t+1] == bob[t]

Next(t) = Transfer(t) // forshadowing

Spec =
  1. Init
  2. all t in Time:
    Next(t) || Stutter(t)

最后，我们如何表示性质 NoOverdrafts？它是一个必须在所有时刻都为真的不变式。因此，我们采用与 Spec 中相同的做法，写出一个针对所有时刻的谓词。Now finally, how do we represent the property NoOverdrafts? It’s an invariant that has to be true at all times. So we do the same thing we did in Spec, write a predicate over all times.

property NoOverdrafts =
  all t in Time:
    alice[t] >= 0

我们甚至可以说 Spec => NoOverdrafts，也就是，如果一个行为在 Spec 下有效，那么它就满足 NoOverdrafts。We can even say that Spec => NoOverdrafts, ie if a behavior is valid under Spec, it satisfies NoOverdrafts.

练习：扩展到 BobExercise: Extending to Bob

修改 Next，让 Bob 也可以向 Alice 转账。不要想得太巧妙，用尽可能直接的方式即可。Modify the Next so that Bob can send Alice transfers, too. Don’t try to be too clever, just do this in the most direct way possible.

附加题：Alice 和 Bob 能在同一个步骤中相互转账吗？Bonus: can Alice and Bob transfer to each other in the same step?

解答Solution

时序逻辑Temporal Logic

这样固然不错，但在实践中，把时间当作一个可以对其量化的集合有两个缺点：This is good and all, but in practice, there’s two downsides to treating time as a set we can quantify over:

  1. 它很繁琐。我们到处都要写 var[t] 和 var[t+1]。It’s cumbersome. We have to write var[t] and var[t+1] all over the place.

  2. 它过于强大。我们可以写出 alice[t^2-5] == alice[t] + t 这样的表达式。It’s too powerful. We can write expressions like alice[t^2-5] == alice[t] + t.

问题 (2) 似乎是件好事；逻辑的整个目的不就是拥有丰富的表达能力吗？但我们心中有一个长远目标：让计算机检查我们的形式化规约。我们需要限制模型的表达能力，使工具能够切实处理它。Problem (2) might seem like a good thing; isn’t the whole point of logic to be expressive? But we have a long-term goal in mind: getting a computer to check our formal specification. We need to limit the expressivity of our model to make it tractable to our tooling.

在实践中，这意味着让时间隐含在模型中，而不是显式地对时间进行量化。In practice, this will mean making time implicit to our model, instead of explicitly quantifying over it.

[[首先，我们需要限制时间的使用方式。]] 在某个给定时刻，我们只能查看变量的当前值（var[t]）和下一个值（var[t+1]）。不能有 var[t+16]、var[t-1]，或其他任何复杂的东西。[[The first thing we need to do is limit how we can use time.]] At a given point in time, all we can look at is the current value of a variable (var[t]) and the next value (var[t+1]). No var[t+16] or var[t-1] or anything else complicated.

而且，我们已经见过表达这种关系的数学惯例：加撇号！对于给定时刻 t，可以规定 var 表示 var[t]，var' 表示 var[t+1]。于是 Transfer(t) 就变成And it turns out we’ve already seen a mathematical convention for expressing this: priming! For a given time t, we can define var to mean var[t] and var' to mean var[t+1]. Then Transfer(t) becomes

Transfer =
  some value in 1..=alice:
    1. alice' == alice - value
    2. bob' == bob + value

我们甚至不再需要把时间作为 Transfer 的参数！主体中带有撇号的谓词有时称为动作。We don’t even need to parameterize Transfer by time anymore! A predicate with primes in the body is sometimes called an action.

练习：用撇号表示停顿Exercise: Stuttering with Primes

重写 Stutter(t)，用撇号代替 t。Rewrite Stutter(t) to use primes instead of t.

解答Solution

接下来，Spec 和 NoOverdrafts 中都有 all t in Time: P(t) 这个结构。换言之，就是“P 始终为真”。因此，我们可以加入一个新术语 always。逻辑学家通常用 □ 或 [] 表示相同的意思。Next we have the construct all t in Time: P(t) in both Spec and NoOverdrafts. In other words, “P is always true”. So we can add always as a new term. Logicians conventionally use □ or [] to mean the same thing.

property NoOverdrafts =
  always (alice >= 0 && bob >= 0)
  // or [](alice >= 0 && bob >= 0)

Spec =
  Init && always (Next || Stutter)

练习：始终算子的规则Exercise: Always rules

这里，我们用 []P 表示 always P。Here we will use []P to mean always P.

  1. 证明 [](all x: P(x)) 与 all x: []P(x) 等价，其中 P 是某种时序谓词（它隐式地接受一个时间参数）。Show that that [](all x: P(x)) is equivalent to all x: []P(x), where P is some sort of temporal predicate (which implicitly takes a time).

  2. 证明 [](P && Q) 与 []P && []Q 相同Show that [](P && Q) is the same as []P && []Q

解答Solution

现在，时间在规约中几乎已经完全隐含起来，只剩一个例外：Init 中有 alice[0] 和 bob[0]。我们只需再加一条约定：如果变量的引用位于时序算子的作用域之外，它就表示 var[0]。由于 Init 位于 [] 之外，它就变成Now time is almost completely implicit in our spec, with just one exception: Init has alice[0] and bob[0]. We just need one more convention: if a variable is referenced outside of the scope of a temporal operator, it means var[0]. Since Init is outside of the [], it becomes

Init =
  1. alice == 10
  2. bob == 10

至此，我们从模型中移除了作为显式值的 Time。And with that, we’ve removed Time as an explicit value in our model.

加入撇号和 always 后，这就成为一种时序逻辑：一种能够对事物随时间变化的方式进行建模的逻辑。因此，它非常适合为软件系统建模。The addition of primes and always makes this a temporal logic: one that can model how things change over time. And that makes it ideal for modeling software systems.

注Note

分析系统并不一定要建立时序逻辑。在 2022 年以前，Alloy 用户通过显式建立 Time 签名来为系统建模。但事实证明，这很繁琐，因此 Alloy 在 2022 年纳入了时序逻辑模型。You don’t have to make a temporal logic to analyze systems. Before 2022, Alloy users modeled systems by making an explicit Time signature. But this proved to be cumbersome, so in 2022 Alloy incorporated a temporal logic model.

无论如何，我们将使用一种从一开始就以时序逻辑为基础设计的规约语言。Regardless, we’ll be using a specification language was that designed with temporal logic from the ground up.

实践：TLA+In Practice: TLA+

为这类并发系统建模时，最流行的规约语言之一是 TLA+。TLA+ 由图灵奖得主 Leslie Lamport 发明，他还发明了各种各样的并发算法和 LaTeX。下面是当前规约的 TLA+ 版本：One of the most popular specification languages for modeling these kinds of concurrent systems is TLA+. TLA+ was invented by the Turing award-winner Leslie Lamport, who also invented a wide variety of concurrency algorithms and LaTeX. Here’s our current spec in TLA+:

代码清单 5 （TLA+）Listing 5 (TLA+)
---- MODULE transfers ----
EXTENDS TLC, Integers

VARIABLES alice, bob
vars == <<alice, bob>>

Init ==
  alice = 10 
  /\ bob = 10

AliceToBob ==
  \E amnt \in 1..alice:
    alice' = alice - amnt
    /\ bob' = bob + amnt

BobToAlice ==
  \E amnt \in 1..bob:
    alice' = alice + amnt
    /\ bob' = bob - amnt

Next ==
  AliceToBob
  \/ BobToAlice

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars \* [](Next \/ Stutter)

NoOverdrafts ==
  [](alice >= 0 /\ bob >= 0)

====

TLA+ 使用数学记法的 ASCII 版本：用 /\ 和 \/ 表示 &&/||，用 \A 和 \E 表示 all/some，等等。== 用于定义，[][Next]_vars 则是 [](Next || Stutter) 的 TLA+ 记法。TLA+ uses ASCII versions of mathematicians notation: /\ and \/ for &&/||, \A and \E for all/some, etc. == is used for definition, and [][Next]_vars is TLA+ notation for [](Next || Stutter).

现在有了规约和性质，我们就可以使用模型检查器生成这个系统所有可能的状态，看看是否有任何状态破坏不变式。与 Alloy 一样，TLA+ 最常见的检查方式是在 VSCode 中使用扩展 [https://github.com/tlaplus/vscode-tlaplus/]。但配置模型运行需要做一些设置，因此我编写了一个名为 tlacli [https://github.com/hwayne/tlacli] 的工具，以便通过命令行完成更多操作。它不支持 TLA+ 的全部功能，但适用于这样的快速演示。Now that we have a specification and a property, we can use a model checker to generate all possible states of this system and see if any of them break our invariant. Like Alloy, TLA+ is most often checked from VSCode via an extension [https://github.com/tlaplus/vscode-tlaplus/]. But setting up a model run takes a bit of configuration, so I created a tool called tlacli [https://github.com/hwayne/tlacli] to do more from the command line. It doesn’t support all of TLA+’s features but is suitable for quick demos like this.

tlacli check transfers.tla --prop NoOverdrafts

结果没有发现错误：And it gets no errors found:

Model checking completed. No error has been found.
421 states generated, 21 distinct states found.

对于这个简单模型，一切都很好，但如果同时有多笔交易正在处理呢？面对并发、非原子的交易，我们的不变式仍然成立吗？So this is all well and good for our simple model, but what if more than one transaction could be in flight at the same time? Does our invariant still work if with concurrent, nonatomic transactions?

加入并发Adding Concurrency

我们可以在“纯”TLA+ 中加入并发，[[但那需要用到一些我现在不想解释的“TLA+ 特有写法”。]] 因此，我们改用 PlusCal，一种可以编译为 TLA+ 的语言。它内置于 TLA+ 工具中，看起来更像编程语言，而不是数学公式，所以很受初学者欢迎。We could add concurrency to our “pure” TLA+, [[but that requires a few “TLA+-isms” I don’t feel like explaining right now.]] So instead we’re going to use PlusCal, a language that compiles to TLA+. It’s built-in with the TLA+ tooling and looks more like programming language than a math formula, so it’s very popular with beginners.

代码清单 6 （TLA+/PlusCal）Listing 6 (TLA+/PlusCal)
---- MODULE transfers2 ----
EXTENDS TLC, Integers

People == {"alice", "bob"}
Money == 1..10
NumTransfers == 2

(* --algorithm wire
variables
  acct \in [People -> Money];

define
  NoOverdrafts ==
    [](\A p \in People:
      acct[p] >= 0)
end define;

process wire \in 1..NumTransfers
variable
  amnt \in 1..5;
  from \in People;
  to \in People
begin
  Check:
    if acct[from] >= amnt then
      Withdraw:
        acct[from] := acct[from] - amnt;
      Deposit:
        acct[to] := acct[to] + amnt;
    end if;
end process;
end algorithm; *)

====

其中大部分看起来像是语法选择有些不同寻常的编程语言，但有些地方需要注意。acct 被设为 [People -> Money] 的任意一个值；这个集合大致包含将 Alice 和 Bob 映射到 1 至 10 之间数值的所有映射。因此，acct 的初值可以是 {alice: 1, bob: 10}、{alice: 3, bob: 6}，或其余 98 种可能组合中的任意一种。Most of this looks like a programming language with some unusual syntactic choices, but there’s some things to pay attention to. acct is set to any value of [People -> Money], roughly the set of all mappings of Alice and Bob to numbers between 1 and 10. So acct can start as {alice: 1, bob: 10}, {alice: 3, bob: 6}, or any of the other 98 possible combinations.

我们的模型在开始时还有两笔不同的汇款同时存在（process wire \in 1..NumTransfers，其中 NumTransfer == 2）。每笔汇款都有各自的 amnt、from 和 to，它们也分别是集合中的元素。不同汇款可以为这些局部值作出不同选择。再结合 amnt，总共有 40,000 种可能的初始状态。Our model also starts with two distinct wires simultaneously (process wire \in 1..NumTransfers where NumTransfer == 2). Each wire has its own amnt, from, and to, which are also individually elements of sets. Different wires can pick different local values for this. Between this and the amnt, there are 40,000 possible initial states.

在 wire 内部，有 Check:、Withdraw: 和 Deposit:。它们是标签，也就是由原子动作组成的组。每笔汇款需要三个步骤才能处理完成：检查余额一步，取款一步，存款一步。粗略估算，两笔 wires 有二十种可能的交错执行方式。更精确地说，要稍少一些，因为有些汇款会在 Check 处提前结束。Inside wire we have Check:, Withdraw:, and Deposit:. These are labels, or groups of atomic actions. Each wire takes three steps to fully process: checking the balance is one step, withdrawing is one step, and depositing is one step. To a first order approximation, there are twenty possible ways the two wires can interleave. More precisely, slightly fewer, because some wires will end early at the Check.

最后，NoOverdrafts 是旧版本的直接翻译，只是推广到了任意数量的用户。Finally, NoOverdrafts is a straight translation of our old version, just generalized to any number of people.

为了把 PlusCal 编译成 TLA+，我运行了 tlacli translate transfers2.tla。翻译在同一文件内完成，结果出现在代码下方。现在进行模型检查，看看 NoOverdrafts 是否仍然成立：To compile the PlusCal to TLA+, I ran tlacli translate transfers2.tla. The translation is done in-file and appears below the code. Now let’s model check it and see if NoOverdrafts still holds:

tlacli check transfers2.tla --prop NoOverdrafts

这样做之后，突然出现了一个错误：If we do this, we suddenly get an error:

Error: Invariant NoOverdrafts is violated.
Error: The behavior up to this point is:
State 1: <Initial predicate>
/\ acct = [alice |-> 1, bob |-> 1]
/\ amnt = <<1, 1>>
/\ to = <<"bob", "alice">>
/\ from = <<"alice", "alice">>
/\ pc = <<"Check", "Check">>

\* four more states after this

这是导致不变式被违反的一条精确事件序列。概括如下：This is an exact sequence of events required to trigger a violated invariant. In summary:

  1. Alice 有 1 美元，并向 Bob 发起两笔各一美元的汇款。Alice has 1 dollar and creates two wires, one dollar each, to Bob.

  2. 汇款 1 执行检查，看到 Alice 至少有一美元，便进入 Withdraw。Wire 1 runs check, sees Alice has at least a dollar, and proceeds to Withdraw.

  3. 在汇款 1 取款之前，汇款 2 执行相同的检查，看到同样的那一美元，也进入 Withdraw。Before wire 1 withdraws, Wire 2 runs the same check, sees the same dollar, and also proceeds to Withdraw.

  4. 两笔汇款各取走一美元，导致 Alice 的余额变成负数。Both wires withdraw one dollar, putting Alice at a negative balance.

这个缺陷之所以出现，是因为检查和取款不是原子的：它们发生在不同的时间步。如果让它们在同一个时间步发生，错误应该就会消失：This bug happens because checking and withdrawing are nonatomic: they happen in different time steps. If we make them happen in the same time step, the error should go away:

begin
- Check:
+ CheckAndWithdraw:
    if acct[from] >= amnt then
-     Withdraw:
        acct[from] := acct[from] - amnt;
+ \* remember to retranslate the file!

重新运行模型检查器，可以看到这个错误不再出现。如果愿意，我们可以把 NumTransfers 设为 6，或再增加三个用户，TLA+ 都能顺畅地检查这个更大的问题。这正是形式化规约对复杂系统如此有用的原因！We can rerun the model checker and see that the error no longer occurs. If we want, we can set NumTransfers to 6 or add another three people, and TLA+ will seamlessly check our larger problem. This is what makes formal specification so useful for complex systems!

活性Liveness

查看翻译结果，你会看到 PlusCal 额外生成了这个性质：If you look at the translation, you’d see this extra property PlusCal generated:

Termination == <>(\A self \in ProcSet: pc[self] = "Done")

ProcSet 是所有汇款的集合（也就是 1..2）。pc 追踪每个进程当前所处的步骤：pc[1] = "Deposit" 表示进程 1 已准备好存款。因此，整个量化表达式就是“每个进程都处于‘Done’步骤”。ProcSet is the set of all wires (so 1..2). pc tracks the current step of each process: pc[1] = "Deposit" means which process 1 is ready to deposit. The whole quantifier is then “every process is at the ‘Done’ step.”

那么 <> 呢？What about the <>?

还记得 [] 是始终，表示 all t in Time 吗？而 <>，即最终，表示的是 some t in Time。Remember how [] was always, and meant all t in Time? <>, or eventually, instead means some t in Time.

Termination =
  some t in Time:
    all self \in ProcSet:
      pc[self][t] = "Done"

<>P 表示 P 不必在开始时就为真，但在所有可能的时间线中，它都必须最终变成真。这就引出了 TLA+ 最强大的功能之一。我们的不变式是一种安全性性质：承诺某种“坏事”不会发生。与之相对的是活性性质：保证某种“好事”会发生。比如，进程最终会完成处理。<>P means that P doesn’t need to be true at the start, but it needs to eventually become true in all possible timelines. This gets to one of the most powerful features of TLA+. Our invariant was a kind of safety property: a promise that something “bad” doesn’t happen. The other half of the coin is the liveness property: something “good” is guaranteed to happen. Like, for example, our processes eventually finish processing.

我们可以用 tlacli check wire.tla --prop Termination 检查 Termination。令人意外的是，它失败了：We can check Termination with tlacli check wire.tla --prop Termination. Surprisingly, it fails:

State 4:
/\ acct = [alice |-> 0, bob |-> 1]
/\ amnt = <<1, 1>>
/\ to = <<"alice", "alice">>
/\ from = <<"alice", "alice">>
/\ pc = <<"Deposit", "Done">>

State 5: Stuttering

“停顿”是 TLA+ 中表示“崩溃”的说法。第一笔汇款几乎完成了，只剩下“Deposit”，却在执行它之前崩溃。Bob 永远也收不到钱。“Stuttering” is TLA+-speak for “crashes”. The first wire is almost finished, it just has to complete “Deposit”, but crashes just before. Bob never gets his money.

默认情况下，TLA+ 假设任何进程都可以在任何步骤崩溃。[[最好先假设情况会尽可能恶劣，再要求用户明确写出自己的假设。]] 如果要声明进程不会崩溃，就必须使其具有“公平性”：By default, TLA+ assumes any process can crash at any step. [[It’s better to assume maximum perversity and force users to make their assumptions explicit.]] If we want to say the process doesn’t crash, we have to make it “fair”:

+ fair process wire \in 1..NumTransfers
- process wire \in 1..NumTransfers

并非所有活性缺陷都能如此轻易地解决。修复活性缺陷往往需要重新思考根本设计。最好在仍处于设计阶段时重新思考，而不是等到产品发布之后。Not all liveness bugs are solved so easily. Often, fixing a liveness bug requires rethinking the fundamental design. Better to do that rethinking while we’re still in the design phase, as opposed to after we released the product.

练习：最终算子的规则Exercise: Eventually rules

  1. 证明 <>some x: P(x) 与 some x: <>P(x) 等价，其中 P 是某种时序谓词（它隐式地接受一个时间参数）。Show that that <>some x: P(x) is equivalent to some x: <>P(x), where P is some sort of temporal predicate (which implicitly takes a time).

  2. 证明 <>(P || Q) 与 <>P || <>Q 相同。Show that <>(P || Q) is the same as <>P || <>Q.

  3. 证明 <>P = ![]!P。Show that <>P = ![]!P.

解答Solution

实际应用中的规约Specification in the wild

过去两章介绍了两种不同的形式化规约语言：TLA+ 和 Alloy。人们了解到这类工具时，通常有两个问题：The past two chapters covered two different formal specification languages: TLA+ and Alloy. When people learn about these kinds of tools, they generally have two questions:

  1. 现实中真的有人用它吗？Is this actually used in the real world?

  2. 我如何确保代码符合规约？How do I make sure my code matches the specification?

第一个问题很容易回答：有很多广受关注的案例研究表明，形式化规约为普通公司节省了大量时间和金钱。我在“延伸阅读”中列出了一些例子。Question one is easy to answer: there are a lot of high-profile case studies of formal specification saving everyday companies a lot of time and money. I’ve put some examples in the “Further Reading” section.

第二个问题更难。正如在功能正确性一章中所见，代码的形式化验证很难。代码需要考虑的事情远比规约多。我们的转账模型抽象掉了从使用的具体软件包到向用户显示的“余额不足”对话框等一切内容。恰恰是这种抽象层次让规约如此强大；验证代码时，这种优势就失去了。Question two is harder. As we’ve seen in the functional correctness chapter, formal verification of code is hard. Code needs to worry about a lot more things than specifications do. Our transfer model abstracted away everything from the specific packages we use to the “insufficient funds” dialog we show to users. That level of abstraction is what makes specification so powerful in the first place; verifying code loses that power.

（确实有一些规约语言能把规约“精化”为代码，例如 Event-B [https://www.event-b.org/]。不过，它们往往难用得多，成本也高得多。）(There are some specification languages that can “refine” spec into code, such as Event-B [https://www.event-b.org/]. These tend to be significantly more difficult and expensive to use, though.)

但形式化规约领域还很年轻，我们已经开始看到一些有趣的发展。在我看来，最令人兴奋的创新是利用形式化规约生成测试。论文《极限建模实践》 [https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.00915]展示了这一点：研究者用 TLA+ 规约为一个 C++ 库生成测试套件。But the field of formal specification is young and we’re starting to see some interesting developments. The most exciting innovation, in my opinion, is using a formal spec to generate tests. You can see ths in the paper eXtreme Modeling in Practice [https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.00915], where they used a TLA+ specification to generate a test suite for a C++ library.

小结Summary

  1. TLA+ 是一种用于为软件系统建模并表达其性质的逻辑。TLA+ is a form of logic used to model software systems and express their properties.

  2. 你可以对 TLA+ 规约进行模型检查，找出违反性质的时间线。You can model check a TLA+ specificaton to find timelines which break properties.

  3. 我们可以检查某个性质是否在所有时间线的所有状态中都为真，或者是否在每条时间线的至少一个状态中为真。We can check that a property is true for all states in all timelines, or at least one state in each timeline.

前两章介绍了形式化规约的两种用途和两种工具。但这只是冰山一角：规约是一个丰富的领域，有各种有趣的语言和应用。我曾用规约语言为概率、机器人、系统动力学模型，乃至公司官僚体系建模！The last two chapters covered two uses of and two tools for formal specification. But this is just the tip of the iceberg: specification is a rich field with all sorts of interesting languages and applications. I’ve worked with specification languages for modeling probability, robotics, system dynamics models, and even corporate bureaucracies!

形式化规约和形式化验证共同构成形式化方法，即直接运用数学来编写代码的学科。我发现，（针对抽象模型的）形式化规约语言比（针对实际代码的）形式化验证语言对业界更有用，主要因为前者更容易学习，融入常规开发流程的成本也低得多。Formal specification and formal verification together for formal methods, the discipline of directly applying math to write code. I’ve found formal specification languages (on abstract models) more useful to industry than formal verification languages (on actual code), mostly because it’s easier to learn and a lot cheaper to incorporate into a regular development workflow.

下一章，我们将暂别形式化方法，转而关注另一类可以用逻辑优雅解决的实际问题。In the next chapter, we will leave formal methods behind and focus on a different class of practical problems elegantly solvable with logic.

求解器Solvers

假设我们有一组 T 个测试，每个测试的运行时间不同。T1 可能需要 1 秒，T2 需要 7 秒，等等。我们可以把测试分配给 N 台相同的服务器。希望通过分配来尽量缩短整体测试时间。如果两台服务器各花 1 秒运行完各自的全部测试，而第三台花了 27 秒，那么整体测试时间就是 27。Let’s say we have a set of T tests, and each takes a different amount of time to run. T1 might take 1 second, T2 7 seconds, etc. We can divide the tests among N identical servers. We want to distribute them to minimize the overall testing time. If two servers take 1 second to run all of its tests and a third takes 27 seconds, the overall testing time is 27.

为了让问题更有意思，某些测试可能属于一个组，而我们希望同组的所有测试都在同一台服务器上运行。To make the problem more interesting, some tests may belong to a group, and we want all tests in the same group to run on the same server.

这类问题很难用普通编程语言求解，却很容易用逻辑表达，并让我们能够用一类新的工具来求解。This kind of problem is difficult to solve in a normal programming language, but it’s very easy to express logically, and lets us use a new class of tools to solve them.

逻辑Logic

通常，我们使用逻辑，是因为它比一般编程语言的表达能力更强。但这次，我们会稍有不同，用一种表达能力更弱的方式写出问题。相信我，这样做是有原因的。Normally, we use logic because it is more expressive than the average programming language. But this time we’ll do things a little differently and write our problem in a less expressive way. Trust me, I have a reason for doing things this way.

首先，如何表示测试时间？用一个 test_times 数组：test_times[2] 是第二个测试所需的时间。与本书其他地方都不同，这里的索引从 1 开始。First, how can we represent the test times? With a test_times array: test_times[2] is the time the second test takes. Unlike everything else in this book, this is 1-indexed.

接下来，如何表示服务器分配？如果规定用整数表示服务器（就像测试一样），那么也可以用数组表示服务器。assignment[5] == 2 表示测试 T5 被分配给服务器 2。Next, how can we represent the server assignments? If we say our servers are represented by integers (just like our tests) we can also represent the server with an array. assignment[5] == 2 means that test T5 is assigned to server 2.

最后，可以用——你猜对了——数组来表示组。group[1] == 2 表示测试 T1 属于组 2。我们还规定不存在“组 0”；group[2] == 0 则表示 T2 不属于任何组。Finally, we can represent the groups as- you guessed it- an array. group[1] == 2 means that test T1 is in group 2. We’ll also say there’s no “group 0”; group[2] == 0 instead means that T2 doesn’t belong to any group.

注意，其中两个数组是“常量”：test_times 和 groups 由外部因素决定。只有 assignment 是“变量”：我们要寻找它满足约束的取值。Notice that two of those arrays are “constants”: the test_times and the groups are fixed by outside forces. Only assignment is a “variable”: we are looking to find its value that satisfies our constraints.

注Note

这里“约束”的含义与数据库一章中的“约束”不同。学科不同，词源也不同。如果我同时用逻辑分析数据库和这类问题，大概会把数据库约束叫作“规则”之类的名称。This is a different meaning of “constraint” than the “constraints” in the database chapter. Different disciplines, different etymologies. If I was logically analyzing both databases and this class of problems at the same time, I’d probably call the database constraints “rules” or something.

分组约束很简单：The group constraint is simple:

constraint GroupsHaveSameAssignment =
  all t1, t2: 1..=T:
    (group[t1] == group[t2] &&
     group[t1] != 0)
    => assignment[t1] == assignment[t2]

（留给读者的练习：为什么不需要检查 group[t2] != 0？）(Exercise for the student: why don’t we need to check group[t2] != 0?)

一台服务器所需的总时间，是分配给它的所有测试耗时的总和。The total time a server takes is the sum of all tests assigned to it.

total_time(s: 1..=S) =
  sum({
    test_times[t]
    for t in 1..T:
      assigment[t] == s
    })

因此，我们的目标是最小化最大的 total_time。Our goal, then, is to minimize the maximum total_time.

minimize max({total_time(s) for s in 1..=S})

实践：求解器In Practice: Solvers

既然已经用逻辑表示了问题，该如何求解呢？Now that we have the problem logically represented, how do we solve it?

当然是使用求解器！By using a solver, of course!

求解器是一种专门寻找这类问题答案的工具。求解器种类繁多，有的针对特定问题，有的用途更广。A solver is a special tool that finds answers to problems like ours. There are all sorts of solvers, some for special problems, some more general purpose.

我们将使用 Minizinc [https://www.minizinc.org/]，纯粹是因为可以免费在线试用 [https://play.minizinc.dev]。你也可以下载到本地运行，这在多数机器上会更快。下面是 MiniZinc 中的解法：We will use Minizinc [https://www.minizinc.org/], purely because you can try it free online [https://play.minizinc.dev]. You can also download it and run it locally, which will be faster on most machines. Here is the solution in MiniZinc:

代码清单 7 （Minizinc）Listing 7 (Minizinc)
int: T = 10; % number tests 
int: S = 2; % number servers
set of int: Servers = 1..S;
set of int: Tests = 1..T;

array[Tests] of int: test_times = [5, 6, 3, 7, 4, 3, 4, 4, 6, 9];
array[Tests] of int: group = [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 0, 1, 0, 0, 2];
array[Tests] of var Servers: assignment;

function var int: total_time(var int: s) =
  sum([test_times[t] | t in Tests where assignment[t] = s]);

constraint forall (t1, t2 in Tests) 
  (group[t1] = group[t2] /\ group[t1] != 0 
    -> assignment[t1] = assignment[t2]);

function var int: num_assigned(var int: s) =
  count(assignment, s);

constraint forall (s1, s2 in 1..S) 
  (abs(count(assignment, s1) - count(assignment, s2)) <= 1);

solve minimize max([total_time(s) | s in 1..S]);

output [
    "Server \(s): \([t | t in Tests where assignment[t] = s])"
       ++ " (\(sum([test_times[t] | t in Tests 
                  where assignment[t] = s])))\n" 
    | s in 1..S
];

与我们见过的其他工具一样，MiniZinc 有自己的逻辑表达式语法，与我们的记法不同。我随意选取了 test_times 和 group 的值；MiniZinc 也可以从数据文件中读取参数。我们必须把 assignment 标为 var，这样 MiniZinc 才知道它可以控制这个值。As with the other tools we have seen, MiniZinc uses its own syntax for logical expressions that is different from ours. I picked arbitrary values for test_times and group; MiniZinc can also read parameters in from a data file. We have to mark assignment as a var so MiniZinc knows it can control that.

运行后，会输出越来越好的结果，直到找到最短时间 26。如果 MiniZinc 找不到任何有效解，就会输出 UNSATISFIABLE。Running this will output progressively better results, until it finds a minimum time of 26. If MiniZinc can’t find any valid solution it will output UNSATISFIABLE.

求解器让我们很容易加入更有趣的约束。例如，可以加一条约束，要求每台服务器上的测试数量大致相同：Solvers make it easy to add more interesting constraints. For example, we can add a constraint that each server must have about the same number of tests:

constraint forall (s1, s2 in 1..S)
  (abs(count(assignment, s1) - count(assignment, s2)) <= 1);

上述问题称为“装箱问题”，是这类求解器最常见的用例之一。只有十个测试时，找到最优解并不太重要，但更真实的工作负载可能有 10,000 个测试！这时求解器就真能替企业省钱了。The above is known as a “bin-packing problem”, which is one of the most popular use-cases for these solvers. Finding the optimium solution doesn’t matter too much with ten tests, but a more realistic workload might be 10,000 tests! That’s when a solver can really save a business money.

速度与表达能力Speed vs Expressiveness

使用 MiniZinc，也解释了为什么我们必须以表达能力如此有限的格式保存参数。MiniZinc 不支持字符串、结构体、数组的数组，也不支持我们在编程语言中习以为常的那些便利功能。即使有这些限制，MiniZinc 的表达能力仍然比许多其他求解器更强。这是因为求解器必须快。对问题中的变量和约束施加的限制越多，求解器就越能专门化，从而越快地求解能够表达的问题。Our use of MiniZinc explains why we had to store our parameters in such an inexpressive format. MiniZinc does not support strings, structures, arrays of arrays, or any of the affordances we’re used to in programming languages. Even with its restrictions, MiniZinc is still more expressive than many other solvers. This because solvers need to be fast. The more restrictions we place on the variables and constraints in our problems, the more specialized our solver can be, and in turn the faster we can solve expressible problems.

例如，线性规划求解器的值只能是数值，而且只能计算形如 a*x1 + b*x2 + ... 的表达式。但专用线性求解器的运行速度可能远高于求解一般的 MiniZinc 问题。For example, a linear programming solver has only numbers for values, and can only compute expressions of the form a*x1 + b*x2 + .... But dedicated linear solvers can run much faster than a general MiniZinc problem.

[[既然如此，如果可行，为什么不把 MiniZinc 问题转换成线性规划问题呢？事实上，它做的正是这件事。MiniZinc 是一种用于表达约束问题的高层、工具无关的语言，它会尝试把问题“编译”为更简单的形式。]][[So why not convert a MiniZinc problem into a linear programming one, if possible? In fact, that’s exactly what it does. MiniZinc is a high-level, tool-agnostic language for expressing constraint problems, which it tries to “compile” into simpler forms.]]

问题和求解器的子类多得令人眼花缭乱，但其中两类尤其值得关注，它们展示了速度与表达能力这条光谱两端可能存在的事物。There’s a dizzying array of subclasses of problems and solvers, but two are of particular interest, showing what can exist on the very ends of the speed/expressiveness spectrum.

注Note

有些类别的问题足够有价值，值得开发专用工具。Google OR-tools [https://developers.google.com/optimization] 是最流行的求解器之一，内含针对调度、车辆路径规划、装箱等问题的专用求解器。Some classes of problems are valuable enough for specialist tools. Google OR-tools [https://developers.google.com/optimization] is one of the most popular solvers available, and has specialized solvers for problems like scheduling, vehicle routing, and bin packing.

SAT 求解器SAT Solvers

如果我们只关心速度，那么能构造出的最精简、最基本的约束语言是什么样的？If all we cared about was speed, what is the most stripped down, barebones constraint language we can make?

把一切都移除，就能得到它。没有字符串、数组、函数，也没有数值。每个变量不是“真”就是“假”。如果要知道测试 7 是否分配给服务器 3，就创建一个布尔变量来追踪这件事。当测试 7 分配给服务器 3 时，a73 为真；未分配给它时，!a73 为真。但这样一来，我们还需要 a72、a71、a63……We get it by removing everything. No strings, arrays, no functions, no numbers. Every variable is “true” or “false”. If we want to see whether test 7 is to server 3, we make a boolean variable tracking that. a73 is true when test 7 is assigned to server 3, !a73 when it isn’t. But then we’ll also need a72, a71, a63…

接着，需要一个约束来表示“每个测试至少分配给一台服务器”。写出这个约束的最简单方式是什么？大概像这样：Then we’ll need a constraint saying “each test is assigned to at least one server.” What’s the simplest possible way to write that constraint? Probably something like this:

(a11 || a12 || a13 ...) &&
(a21 || a22 || a23 ...) &&
(a31 || a32 || a33 ...) &&

（这种“多个或式的与”通常称为合取范式，简称 CNF。）(This “AND of ORs” is conventionally called Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF).)

看起来不错。但没有任何东西阻止 a11 和 a12 同时为真：测试 1 被分配给了两台不同的服务器！因此，我们还需要声明：“如果测试 1 分配给了 1，就不能同时分配给 2 或 3”：Looks good. But there’s nothing stopping a11 and a12 from both being true at the same time: test 1 is assigned to two different servers! So we also need to say “if test 1 is assigned to 1, it cannot also be assigned to 2 or 3”:

(a11 && !a12 && !a13 ...) ||
(!a11 && a12 && !a13 ...) ||

但这样一来，求解器必须既理解“多个或式的与”，又理解“多个与式的或”。表达能力太强了！最好设法将其改写成 CNF：But now our solver has to understand both “AND of ORs” and “OR of ANDs”. That’s too much expressivity! Better find a way to rewrite that in CNF:

(!a11 || !a12) &&
(!a11 || !a13) &&
(!a12 || !a13) &&
...

练习Exercise

解释为什么这意味着测试 1 不能分配给两台不同的服务器。Explain why this means test 1 can’t be assigned to two different servers.

解答Solution

求解这种形式的问题的工具称为 SAT 求解器，名称来自“布尔可满足性”（Boolean SATisfiability）。语法或许显得受限，但能转换成 SAT 问题的问题数量多得惊人。作为回报，SAT 求解器是世界上最快的一类求解器，处理数 GB 大小的问题是家常便饭。Solvers for problems of this form are called SAT solvers, after “Boolean SATisfiability”. The syntax may seem constrained, but a surprisingly large number of problems can be transformed into SAT problems. And in return, SAT solvers are some of the fastest solvers in the world, routinely handling problems gigabytes in size.

注Note

也许可以加一道把标签规则转换为 SAT 的练习。无需真的把标签做成参数，只需用子句替代即可。Maybe an exercise on converting the tag rule to SAT. We don’t need to actually make the tags parameters, just replace them with clauses.

注Note

所有能由 SAT 求解器求解的问题组成的集合，就是因 P vs NP 而闻名的“NP 复杂度类”。NP 被认为是“难处理的”，意思是我们没有高效算法来求解这一类中的所有问题。实际遇到的大多数 SAT 问题都“表现良好”，能很快求解。但也有很小的 SAT 问题，穷尽人的一生也求不出来。The set of all problems solvable by a SAT solver is the “NP complexity class”, of P vs NP fame. NP is considered “intractable”, meaning we do not have efficient algorithms to solve all of the problems in the class. Most SAT problems seen in the wild are “well-behaved” and can be solved quickly. But you can also find small SAT problems that can’t be solved in a human lifetime.

因此，许多人使用能接受表达能力丰富的形式并将其转换为 SAT 的工具。你可以把 SAT 想象成一种低层“汇编”语言，其他工具把问题“编译”成它。Alloy 内部就使用 SAT 求解器。For this reason, many people use tools that take expressive forms and convert them into SAT. You can think of SAT as a low level “assembly” language that other tools “compile” to. Alloy uses a SAT solver internally.

SMT 求解SMT

在表达能力的另一端，是 SMT，即可满足性模理论（Satisfiability Modulo Theories）求解器。其他求解器针对受限类别的数学问题，而 SMT 求解器很灵活，能处理多种不同问题。举一个例子，我们可以用它逆向分析随机数生成器（RNG）。On the other end of expressivity, we have SMT, or Satisfiability Modulo Theories solver. While other solvers target a restricted category of math problem, SMT solvers are flexible and handle a wide range of different problems. As just one example, we can use it to reverse engineer a random number generator (RNG).

一种较早的随机数生成器是线性同余生成器，简称 LCG。从种子值 x_0 开始，每个后续值由 x_n+1 = (a*x_n + c) % m 确定，其中 (a, c, m) 都是固定值。给定一个序列和 m，能否恢复出 (a, c)？目前最流行的 SMT 工具是 Z3 [https://microsoft.github.io/z3guide/]。One old type of random number generator is the Linear Congruential Generator, or LCG. Starting with a seed value x_0, each next value is determined by x_n+1 = (a*x_n + c) % m, where (a, c, m) are all fixed values. Given a sequence and m, can we recover (a, c)? The most popular SMT in use is Z3 [https://microsoft.github.io/z3guide/].

代码清单 8 （Python）Listing 8 (Python)
# requires `pip install z3-solver`
from z3 import *
solver = Solver()

modulus = eval(input("Enter modulus: "))
sequence = eval(input("Enter sequence: ")) # Separate with commas

a = Int('a')
c = Int('c')

solver.add(a >= 0, a < modulus)
solver.add(c >= 0, c < modulus)

for i in range(len(sequence) - 1):
    solver.add(sequence[i+1] == c + (a * sequence[i]) % modulus)

if solver.check() == sat:
    model = solver.model()
    print(f"a = {model[a].as_long()}")
    print(f"c = {model[c].as_long()}")
else:
    print("Could not find parameters")

运行代码时的情况如下：Here is what it looks like to run the code:

Enter modulus: 2**31
Enter sequence: 4096, 618876929, 113892918, 1048278319
a = 22695477
c = 1

SMT 的表达能力甚至超过“通用”约束求解器，但代价是完备性。前面看到的所有约束问题都是可判定的，也就是说，求解器要么一定返回一个值，要么一定告诉我们无解。SMT 求解器还可能返回“UNKNOWN”，表示它连问题到底有没有解都无法确定。随着时间推移，SMT 求解器越来越擅长寻找解，但它们永远不可能解决所有问题。这就是表达能力的代价。SMT are more expressive than even “generic” constraint solvers, but that expressiveness comes at a price of completeness. All of the prior constraint problems we looked at were decidable, meaning the solver will either definitely return a value or definitely tell us there is no solution. SMT solvers can also return “UNKNOWN”, meaning the solver couldn’t figure if the problem is even solvable or not. Over time, SMT solvers are getting better and better at finding solutions, but they will never be able to solve all problems. Such is the price of expressiveness.

尽管如此，SMT 求解器凭借灵活性极受欢迎，用途多种多样。它们可以破解密码学原语 [https://github.com/kste/cryptosmt]、逆向分析已编译的二进制文件 [https://docs.angr.io/en/latest/core-concepts/solver.html]、找出防火墙规则集之间的差异 [https://github.com/Z3Prover/FirewallChecker]，以及从规约合成代码 [https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~npolikarpova/publications/popl20.pdf]。它们还是多数定理证明和形式化验证工作的驱动引擎。Dafny 用 SMT 求解器验证代码，一款研究性质的 TLA+ 模型检查器也是如此。Nonetheless, SMT solvers are incredibly popular for their flexibility and see all sorts of different use cases. They can crack cryptographic primitives [https://github.com/kste/cryptosmt], reverse engineer compiled binaries [https://docs.angr.io/en/latest/core-concepts/solver.html], find differences in firewall rulesets [https://github.com/Z3Prover/FirewallChecker], and synthesize code from specifications [https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~npolikarpova/publications/popl20.pdf]. They are also the engine that powers most work in theorem proving and formal verification. Dafny uses an SMT solver to verify code, and one research model checker for TLA+ does too.

注Note

求解器（判断是否存在解）怎么能驱动验证器（检查某个性质是否始终成立）呢？很简单，利用量词对偶性即可。如果性质是 all x: P(x)，就让求解器满足 !P(x)。如果求解器找不到任何解，那么 !(some x: !P(x)) 就成立，而它与原性质等价。How can a solver (which finds if solutions exist) power a verifier (which checks that a property always holds)? Easy, just exploit quantifier duality. If the property is all x: P(x), then ask the solver to satisfy !P(x). If the solver can’t find any solutions, then !(some x: !P(x)) holds, which is equivalent to our property.

该用哪一种？Which to use?

面对所有这些选项，该选择哪种求解器？这取决于很多因素，但我可以给出一些非常概括的经验法则。So given all of the options, which solver is the right one to pick? This depends on a lot of factors, but I can provide some very general heuristics.

首先，多数程序员不太可能直接使用 SAT。SAT 又快又强大，但要以最优方式表示问题，并把 SAT 的解解释成原问题的解，都需要很高的技巧。因此，SAT 求解器的主要用户是这样的人：1) 绝对需要把问题的性能推到极致，或者 2) 正在构建更高层的工具。我们更可能使用某种内部以 SAT 求解器作为实现一部分的工具。First of all, most programmers are unlikely to directly use SAT. SAT is fast and powerful but it takes a lot of skill to represent problems in an optimal way, and to interpret a SAT solution to a problem. For these reasons, the main users of SAT solvers are people who 1) absolutely need the maximum possible performance on their problem, or 2) are building higher-level tools. We are more likely to use a tool that uses a SAT solver as part of its implementation.

其次，合适的求解器取决于目标的性质：是满足约束，还是优化？问题的解很少，而且找到任意一个都可以时，SMT 求解器就是合适的工具。问题有许多有效解，但某些解比其他解更优时，其他求解器才是合适的工具。粗略来说，大多数“满足约束”问题偏向技术或“软件工程”，而大多数优化问题偏向业务或“运筹学”：排班、车辆路径规划、制造优化、资源分配等。After that, the right solver depends on the nature of our goal: is it satisfaction or optimization? SMT solvers are the right tool when the problem has very few solutions and any one will do. Other solvers are the right tool when the problem has many valid solutions, but some are more optimal than others. As a rough rule, most “satisfaction” problems are technical/”software engineering”-oriented, while most optimization problems are business/”operations research”-oriented: shift scheduling, vehicle routing, manufacturing optimization, resource allocation, etc.

如果 SMT 是合适的选择，就默认使用 Z3。在所有 SMT 求解器中，它得到的支持最广，与最多的语言集成，文档也最详尽。If SMT is the right choice, then we default to Z3. It is most widely supported, has integrations with the most languages, and has the most thorough documentation of any SMT solver.

如果应该选用优化求解器，一般做法是找到能够完整表达问题、但表达能力最弱的那类工具，因为它会最快。[[ILP、LP、Simplex、MIP 等。]] 工具和类别多得令人眼花缭乱。MiniZinc 和 Google 的 OR-Tools [https://developers.google.com/optimization] 是还不错的起点。If an optimization solver is the right choice, the general approach is to find the least expressive class of tools that totally expresses the problem, as that will be the fastest. [[ILP, LP, Simplex, MIP, etc]]. There’s a dizzying plethora of different tools and classes. A decent enough starting point is MiniZinc and Google’s OR-Tools [https://developers.google.com/optimization].

小结Summary

  • 有些类别的问题很难以程序方式表达，却能用求解器高效求解。There are classes of problems that are difficult to express programmatically, but are solved efficiently with solvers.

  • 求解器表达约束问题的便利程度与求解速度之间存在取舍。There is a tradeoff between how easily a solver can express constraint problems and how quickly it can solve them.

  • SAT 求解器速度快，但表达能力很弱。它们是许多高层软件中的核心低层组件。SAT solvers are fast but very inexpressive. They are a core low-level component in a lot of higher-level software.

  • SMT 求解器表达能力强，但不完备。它们也被广泛使用，既可直接使用，也可作为低层组件。SMT solvers are expressive but incomplete. They are also widely used, both directly and as low-level components.

  • SAT 和 SMT 求解器主要用于“满足约束”问题，其他求解器则主要用于“优化”问题。SAT and SMT solvers are primarily used for “satisfaction” problems, while other solvers are primarily used for “optimization” problems.

下一章将介绍最名副其实的“逻辑编程”。The next chapter is about the most literal kind of “logic programming”.

逻辑编程Logic Programming

在一本叫《程序员的逻辑学》的书里，我竟然成功地写了九十页都没有提起“逻辑编程”。我觉得自己值得一枚奖章。In a book called “Logic for Programmers” I’ve somehow managed to not bring up “logic programming” for ninety pages. I feel like I deserve a medal.

逻辑编程（LP）是一种独立的编程范式，就像命令式和函数式编程一样。最著名的逻辑编程语言叫作“Prolog”。Prolog 最初诞生于 1970 年代，此后衍生出许多不同变体。我们将使用“SWI-Prolog”变体，你可以在 https://swish.swi-prolog.org/ 在线试用。受篇幅所限，本章只能比其他章节更侧重于概览。Logic programming (LP) is a distinct paradigm of programming, like imperative and functional are. The most famous logic programming language is called “Prolog”. Prolog was first created in 1970s and since then has split off into many different variants. We will use the “SWI-Prolog” variant, which you can try online at https://swish.swi-prolog.org/. By necessity, this chapter will be even more of a broad overview than the other chapters.

Prolog 语言Prolog

Prolog 程序有三种基本构件：There are three basic building blocks of a Prolog program:

  1. 原子是以小写字母开头的值标识符（bread、flour）。它们是不含变量的符号：bread 只等于 bread，不等于其他任何东西。Atoms are value identifiers that start with a lower-case letter (bread, flour). These are ground symbols: bread is equal to bread and nothing else.

  2. 变量是以大写字母开头的标识符（X、Abc）。Prolog 程序的最终目标是把变量“合一”到能使谓词为真的值。Variables are identifiers that start with a capital (X, Abc). The ultimate goal of a Prolog program is to “unify” variables to values that would make predicates true.

  3. 谓词，可以对特定的原子为真，也可以对满足某个条件的原子为真。这两种谓词分别称为事实和规则。Predicates, which can be true for specific atoms, or for atoms that pass a condition. These predicates are called facts and rules, respectively.

% comments start with %
ingredient(bread, flour). % don't forget the period!
ingredient(bread, water).

这定义了事实 ingredient()，并规定当第一个参数为 bread，第二个参数为 flour 或 water 时，它为真。现在，如果我用变量调用 ingredient，就是在请求 Prolog 引擎找出一个能使表达式为真的值。This defines the fact ingredient() and determines it’s true if the first parameter is bread and the second is flour or water. Now if I call ingredient with a variable, I am asking the Prolog engine to find a value that makes my expression true.

ingredient(X, flour).
X = bread % result

ingredient(X, potatoes).
false % no possible X

这直接对应 some 量词：若 some x:  ingredient(x, flour)，则 ingredient(X, flour) 为真。如果有多个值满足表达式，Prolog 会逐个返回可能的值。This maps directly to the some quantifier: ingredient(X, flour) is true if some x:  ingredient(x, flour). If multiple values satisfy the expression, then Prolog will return possible values one at a time.

表示食谱并不是常见的编程任务，所以我们继续看一个更实际的例子。很少有人在工作中处理食谱，但几乎人人都使用版本控制，而提交之间的关系可以直接用事实表达：Representing recipes are not a common programming task, so let us continue with a more practical example. Few people work with recipes in their job, but almost everyone uses version control, and the relationships between commits is directly expressible in facts:

parent(a0, a1).
parent(a1, a2).
parent(a2, a3).
parent(a3, a4).
parent(a4, a5).
parent(a1, b1).
parent(b1, b2).
parent(b2, a4).
parent(b2, b3).

这表示图 5中的提交图。This represents the commit graph in Fig. 5.

有了一组事实，就可以加入“规则”，也就是主体较复杂的谓词。例如，“合并提交”是有两个不同父提交的提交。Once we have a collection of facts, we can then add “rules”, or predicates with complex bodies. For example, a “merge commit” is one that has two different parents.

mergecommit(C) :-
    parent(P1, C),
    parent(P2, C),
    \+ (P1 = P2). % \+ is 'not'

?- mergecommit(C).
C = a4.

规则可以有多个定义，此时只要任意一条规则为真，谓词就为真。这使递归陈述很容易表达，例如：“如果 A 是 C 的父提交，或者是 C 的某个祖先提交的父提交，那么 A 就是 C 的祖先提交。”Rules can have multiple definitions, in which case the predicate is true if any rule is true. This makes it easy to express recursive statements, like “A is the ancestor of C if it is a parent of C or the parent of an ancestor of C.”

ancestor(A, Commit) :- parent(A, Commit).
ancestor(A, Commit) :- 
    parent(A, Y),
    ancestor(Y, Commit).

有了这些，我们就能表达复杂查询，例如“提交 A 的祖先中，不是提交 B 的祖先的那些提交”：With this, we can express complex queries, like “ancestors of commit A that are not ancestors of commit B”:

% \+ is "not"
?- ancestor(a5, X), \+ ancestor(b3, X).
X = a4 ;
X = a3 ;
X = a2

注Note

Prolog 使用“回溯”算法寻找解。因此，它不保证返回的所有解都互不重复。Prolog uses a “backtracking” algorithm to find solutions. As such, it does not guarantee that all solutions are unique.

LP 语言是通用语言，能做命令式或函数式语言能做的一切。问题在于，这种范式在哪些方面比其他编程范式做得更好？曾经，答案是“人工智能”，逻辑编程在很大程度上被视为专家系统和自然语言处理的最佳工具。如今，这一地位已大多被机器学习和大语言模型等统计方法取代。LP languages are general-purpose languages and can do everything that can be done in an imperative or functional language. The question is what can this paradigm do better than other programming paradigms? At one time, the answer was “artificial intelligence”, and logic programming was largely seen as the best tool for expert systems and natural language processing. This niche has been largely superceded by statistical methods like machine learning and large language models.

但它仍有用武之地。本章末尾的“延伸阅读”列出了一些实际应用案例。而且在某些细分领域，逻辑编程仍普遍是首选方法。But there are still places where it sees use. Some specific use cases in the wild are listed in the “Further Reading” at the end of this chapter. And there are still some niches where logic programming is broadly the preferred approach.

演绎数据库Deductive Databases

演绎数据库是另一种形式的数据库。它不把数据存储在表中，而是存储为事实和规则。此时，逻辑编程纯粹成了查询工具，而非通用编程手段。前面的提交模型可以说就是一个演绎数据库。要给提交加入新信息，只需增加新事实：A deductive database is an alternate form of database. Instead of storing data in tables, deductive databases store data as facts and rules. Logic programming then becomes purely a tool for querying, as opposed to general programming. Our previous commit model is arguably a deductive database. Adding new information to the commits is as easy as adding new facts:

% commit(id, author, [files_changed])
% written this way to be more compact
commit(a0, alice, [file(f1), file(f2), testfile(f2)]).
commit(a1, bob, [file(f1), file(f3), testfile(f1)]).
commit(a2, eve, [file(f1), file(f2), testfile(f1), testfile(f2)]).

% commit_author_file
caf(C, A, F) :-
    commit(C, A, Files),
    member(F, Files).

file(f1) 是 Prolog 的复合项，相当于其他语言中的结构体或积类型。它可以用于[[模式匹配]]：caf(_, alice, testfile(X)) 会检索 Alice 修改过的所有测试文件（但不包括普通文件）。file(f1) is a prolog compound term, equivalent to a struct or product type in other languages. It can be used in [[pattern matching]]: caf(_, alice, testfile(X)) will retrieve any testing file (but not regular file) that Alice modified.

[[过渡段]][[bridge]]

[[在论文《基于证据的故障预测》中，Nagappan 等人认为，文件变更的模式可以预测这些文件出现缺陷的可能性。提交次数更多、即“变更频繁”的文件，更可能存在潜在缺陷。让我们实现两条规则，用来提示某个文件更可能存在缺陷：]][[In their paper Evidence Based Failure Prediction, Nagappan et al argue that patterns in how we change files can predict the likelihood of bugs in those files. Files with more commits, “churn”, are more likely to have latent bugs. Let’s implement two rules that suggest a file is more likely to have bugs:]]

  1. 当一个文件至少被三次不同提交修改，且这些提交来自不同作者时，high_churn 为真。在我们的模型中，只有 file(f1) 符合。high_churn is true if a file was changed by at least three different commits with different authors. In our model, this applies to just file(f1).

  2. 当一个文件在某次提交中被修改，而对应的测试没有被修改时，untested_commit 为真。这项检查不应适用于测试文件。在我们的模型中，file(f1) 和 file(f3) 符合。untested_commit is true if a file was changed in a commit, and its corresponding test was not changed. This check should not apply to test files. In our model, this applies to file(f1) and file(f3).

high_churn(File) :-
    caf(_, A1, File), caf(_, A2, File), caf(_, A3, File),
    A1 @< A2, A2 @< A3. % @< = ordering on atoms

untested_commit(file(File)) :-
    commit(_, _, Files),
    member(file(File), Files),
    \+ member(testfile(File), Files).

我们可以更优雅地编写 high_churn（也不必硬编码作者数量），但那需要更高级的 Prolog 技巧。在此基础上，可以将每个文件映射到它未通过的检查数量。We can write high_churn more elegantly (and not hardcode in the number of authors), but that requires more sophisticated Prolog technique. From here, we can map each file to the number of checks it fails.

% fails_check just calls the check on the file
% Added for descriptivity
fails_check(File, Check) :- call(Check, File).

checks_failed(_, [], []).
checks_failed(File, [Check|Checks], Failed) :- 
  checks_failed(File, Checks, Failed), 
  \+ fails_check(File, Check).

checks_failed(File, [Check|Checks], [Check|Failed]) :- 
  checks_failed(File, Checks, Failed), 
  fails_check(File, Check).

checks_failed(File, Failed) :- 
  checks_failed(File, [high_churn, untested_commit], Failed).

如果只想得到每个文件未通过的检查数，可以再写一个辅助运算符。If we just want the count of the checks each file failed, we can write another helper operator.

file_suspicion(File, Suspicion) :-
    checks_failed(File, Failed),
    length(Failed, Suspicion).

实践中，Prolog 很少用作演绎数据库的查询语言，原因有二：Prolog 无法嵌入其他语言，而且 Prolog 查询不保证终止。主要使用的语言是 Datalog，这是 Prolog 中“表现良好”、没有这些问题的一个子集。例如，Datomic [https://www.datomic.com/] 使用 Datalog 查询，但将其作为 DSL 嵌入 Clojure。In practice, Prolog is rarely used as the query language for deductive databases for two reasons: Prolog cannot be embedded in other languages, and Prolog queries are not guaranteed to terminate. The main language is instead Datalog, a “well-behaved” subset of Prolog without these issues. Datomic [https://www.datomic.com/], for example, uses datalog for queries, but embeds it as a DSL in Clojure.

约束逻辑编程Constraint Logic Programming
