规划Planning

有一类 AI 问题（截至 2025 年）无法用统计方法处理：规划。给定起始状态、一组有效动作和目标状态，什么样的动作序列能让我们到达目标状态？There is one class of AI problems that (as of 2025) cannot be handled with statistical approaches: planning. Given a starting state, a set of valid actions, and a goal state, what sequence of actions should get us to the goal state?

考虑如下情形：有一组在线服务器，需要进行两次操作系统更新。我们只能升级离线服务器，而且必须确保始终至少有一台服务器在线。可以进一步抽象服务器，让它只包含一个名称、一个表示开关状态的布尔值，以及一个数值版本号。Consider the following situation: we have a set of online servers that need two OS updates. We can only upgrade a server that is offline, and we need to make sure that we always have at least one server online. We can further abstract the servers so that they consist only of a name, a boolean on/off state, and a numerical version.

这种情况下，两台服务器的起始状态是集合 {(s1, on, 1), (s2, on, 1)，目标状态是 {(s1, on, 3), (s2, on, 3)，有两种可能的动作：In this case, the starting state for two servers would be the set {(s1, on, 1), (s2, on, 1), the goal state would be {(s1, on, 3), (s2, on, 3), and there would be two possible actions:

  • 切换一台服务器的状态，除非这样会导致所有服务器都关闭Toggle the state of a server, unless doing so would leave all servers off

  • 将一台关闭的服务器的版本号递增。Increment the version of an off server.

Prolog 本身不支持规划，但我个人最喜欢的逻辑语言 Picat [http://picat-lang.org/] 支持。下面是 Picat 中的规划问题：Prolog does not natively support planning, but my personal favorite logic language, Picat [http://picat-lang.org/], does. Here is the planning problem in Picat:

代码清单 9 （Picat）Listing 9 (Picat)
import planner, math, util.

final(N) =>
  foreach($server(_, State, Version) in N)
    State = on, Version = 3
  end.

cost(State) = 1.

% At least one server online
valid(State) => member($server(_, on, _), State). 

action(From, To, Action, Cost) ?=> % toggle state
  member(X, From), 
  (
   Action = $off(X[1]), To = replace(From, X, X.replace(on, off));
   Action = $on(X[1]), To = replace(From, X, X.replace(off, on))
  ), 
  valid(To), 
  Cost = cost(From).

action(From, To, Action, Cost) => % increment version
  member(X, From),
  X = $server(Name, off, Version),
  To = replace(From, X, X.replace_at(3, Version+1)),
  Action = $upgrade(Name),
  Cost = cost(From).

main =>
  Start = [$server(s1, on, 1), $server(s2, on, 1)],
  best_plan(Start, Plan, Cost),
  writeln(Plan), writeln(Cost).

运行后得到：Running this gives me:

[off(s1), upgrade(s1), upgrade(s1), on(s1),
 off(s2), upgrade(s2), upgrade(s2), on(s2)]
 8

我在代码中让第一项输出表示解决问题的步骤列表。第二项输出是计划的“成本”，Picat 会自动将其最小化。在这里，每个动作的成本为 1，意味着总成本就是计划中的步骤数。I coded the first output to be the list of steps that solves our problems. The second output is the “cost” of the plan, which Picat will automatically minimize. In this case, each action has cost 1, meaning to total cost is just the number of steps in our plan.

规划器能自动找到解决问题的步骤序列，还能最小化成本。在这个例子中，“成本”只是步骤数，因此得到一个八步解。为了展示其能力，我们可以在多台在线服务器版本不同时加入额外惩罚，数值等于 (MaxVersion - MinVersion) 的立方。The planner is automatically able to find a sequence of steps that solves our problem. It can also minimize cost. In this case, the “cost” is just the number of steps, leading to an eight-step solution. To showcase we can add an additional penalty for having several online servers with different versions, equal to (MaxVersion - MinVersion) cubed.

程序看起来非常相似：Our program looks very similar:

- cost(State) = 1.
+ cost(State) = Out =>
+   member($server(_, on, Vmin), State).minof(Vmin),
+   member($server(_, on, Vmax), State).maxof(Vmax),
+   Out = 1 + max(0, Vmax - Vmin)**3.

做出这些修改后，八步解的总成本将是 16。Picat 则会找到步骤更多、但成本更低的解：With these changes, the eight-step solution would have a total cost of 16. Picat, instead, finds a longer solution with a smaller cost:

[off(s1), upgrade(s1), on(s1),
 off(s2), upgrade(s2), upgrade(s2), on(s2),
 off(s1), upgrade(s1), on(s1)]
 12

规划主要用于 AI 研究，尤其是电子游戏 AI，在那里它被称为目标导向动作规划。Planning is mostly used in AI research and especially in video game AIs, where it is called Goal-Oriented Action Planning.

小结Summary

  • 逻辑编程把程序表达为谓词，让用户寻找满足这些谓词的值。最著名的 LP 语言是 Prolog。Logic programming express programs as predicates and allow users to find values that match those predicates. The most famous LP language is Prolog.

  • LP 也可以用于查询所谓“演绎数据库”中的数据。最著名的 LP 查询语言是 Datalog。LP can also be used for querying data in so-called “deductive databases”. The most famous LP query language is Datalog.

  • 规划器编程寻找能将起始状态变为目标状态的动作序列。Picat 就是一种这样的规划语言。Planner programming find sequences of actions that change a starting state into a goal state. One such planning language is Picat.

数学记法Math Notation

本书自始至终使用程序员熟悉的符号和我自己的语法；数学家使用的符号则不同。我这样做，是希望一切都能方便地用 grep 搜索，并能从上下文推断含义。如果你第一次见到 ∪，要查出它的意思可真不容易！I used programmer symbols and my own syntax through this book; mathematicians use different symbols. 量化表达式Quantified Expressions

以表达式 all x in set: P(x) 为例。数学家有三种不同的写法：Take the expression all x in set: P(x). Here are three different ways mathematicians write it:

公式：∀x ∈ set: P(x) EQN: ∀x ∈ set: P(x)

公式：∀x. set(x) → P(x) EQN: ∀x. set(x) → P(x)

公式：∀x: set | P(x) EQN: ∀x: set | P(x)

有些数学家用 ∃!x 表示“恰好存在一个 x”，但这绝不是通用的约定。Some mathematicians write ∃!x to mean “there exists exactly one x”, but it’s not by any means a universal convention.

重言式Tautologies

我把双重否定重写规则写成 !!P = P。更精确地用数学语言说，给定 !!P，就能证明 P。你可以用三种方式写出它：I wrote the double negative rewrite rule as !!P = P. To be more mathematically precise, given !!P, we can prove P. Three ways you could write this:

数学家采用哪一种，可能取决于其论文发表所属的具体领域。在最后一种情况下，他们会保留 → 来表示“我们可以证明”，并且只用 ⇒ 表示“蕴含”。Which one a mathematician uses can depend on the particular field they publish in. In the last case, they will reserve → to mean “we can prove” and exclusively use ⇒ to mean “implies”.

重言式表Table of Tautologies

其中一些使用 =，表示两个公式等同，可以相互替换。另一些使用 =>，表示只能沿一个方向推导。Some of these are =, to mean the two formulas are identical- you can substitute one for the other. Some are =>, meaning they only go one way.

命题逻辑：Propositional Logic:

P = !!P

P && !P = False
P || !P = True

德摩根律：De Morgan’s law:

!P && !Q = !(P || Q)
!P || !Q = !(P && Q)

!P && Q = !(P || !Q)

蕴含Implication

定义：Definition:

P => Q = !P || Q
!(P => Q) = P && !Q

逆否命题：Contrapositive:

P => Q = !Q => !P

(P => Q) && (Q => P) = (P = Q)

传递性：(P => Q && Q => R) => (P => R) 注意，这里不是 =！它不能双向推导！Transitivity: (P => Q && Q => R) => (P => R) Note it’s not an =! It doesn’t go both ways!

量词Quantifiers

提取：Extraction:

all x: P &&/|| Q(x) = P &&/|| all x: Q(x)

对偶：Duals:

all x: P(x) = !(some x: !P(x))
some x: P(x) = !(all x: !P(x))

all x: !P(x) = !(some x: P(x))
some x: !P(x) = !(all x: P(x))

交换性：Commutativity:

all x in S: (all y in T: ...) =

all x in S, y in T: ...

all x in S, y in S: ... =
all x, y in S: ...

some y in T: (some x in S: ...) =
some x in S, y in T: ...

some x, y in S: ...

some x: all y 可以替换为 all y: some x，后者更强。不能反向替换！some x: all y can be replaced with all y: some x, which is stronger. You cannot go the other way!

整本书讨论的都是经典一阶逻辑。这是多数数学家用来做数学的逻辑。但数学是灵活的，而且数学家不喜欢把一个体系视为理所当然。因此，许多数学家都问过：“如果我们改变逻辑，会发生什么？”This entire book is about classical first order logic. That’s the logic that most mathematicians use to do math. But mathematics is flexible and mathematicians hate taking a system for granted. So many mathematicians have asked “what happens if we make logic different?”

这里介绍其中一些改变逻辑的方式。This is some of about those ways of making logic different.

边界：罗素悖论The Limit: Russell’s Paradox

对于每个集合 s，我们都可以创建一个谓词 S(x) = x in s。这意味着每个集合都定义了一个谓词。反过来也成立吗：对于每个谓词，能否找到由所有满足该谓词的事物组成的集合？For every set s, we can create a predicate S(x) = x in s. This means every set defines a predicate. Is the opposite true: for every predicate, can we find a set of all things that pass that predicate?

CanRunProgram(c) = RAM(c) && (CPU(c) || GPU(c))

->

CanRunProgram = RAM & (CPU | GPU)

在朴素集合论中，这对所有集合都成立。但朴素集合论存在一个问题，导致数学家在一个多世纪前放弃了它。考虑谓词 Evil(x) = x not in x，也就是 x 不是包含自身的集合。大多数集合都满足这个谓词：{}、{1}、{[1, 3], abc}，等等。有些集合不满足它，比如“所有非空集合组成的集合”。如果所有谓词都能形成集合，反之亦然，那么我们就会有一个集合 evil，即由所有不包含自身的集合组成的集合。In naive set theory, this is true for all sets. Naive set theory has a problem, though, that lead to mathematicians abandoning it over a century ago. Consider the predicate Evil(x) = x not in x, aka x is not a set that contains itself. Most sets would pass this predicate: {}, {1}, {[1, 3], abc}, etc. Some sets would fail this predicate, like “the set of all non-empty sets”. If all predicates formed sets and vice versa, we’d have a set evil, the set of all sets that don’t contain themselves.

那么 Evil(evil) 为真吗？如果为真，evil 就不包含自身，这意味着它不属于 evil，所以根据定义，Evil(evil) 为假；但这样它又不属于 evil，意味着它不包含自身，也就意味着 Evil(evil) 为真……Now is Evil(evil) true? If so, evil doesn’t contain itself, meaning it’s not in evil, so Evil(evil) is false by definition, but then it’s not in evil, meaning it doesn’t contain itself, meaning Evil(evil) is true…

这称为“罗素悖论”，被视为并非所有谓词都能形成集合的一个理由。为了寻找避免这一悖论的方法，它推动了 20 世纪早期形式逻辑的许多发展。最主流的解决方案称为“ZF”集合论，另一种则是现代类型论，它已在现代函数式 proThis is called “Russell’s paradox” and is considered a reason that not all predicates form sets. The paradox drove much of the development of formal logic in the early 20th century in order to find ways to avoid the paradox. The most mainstream solution to this is called “ZF” Set Theory, but another is modern type theory, which has found a home in modern functional pro

高阶逻辑Higher Order Logic

在本书前面，我写过Early in the book I wrote

为了避免诡异的数学恐怖，谓词不能属于论域：不存在以其他谓词为参数的谓词。So as to prevent eldritch math horrors, predicates cannot be in the domain of discourse: there are no predicates that take other predicates.

这使我们的逻辑成为一阶逻辑。在高阶逻辑中，谓词既可以作为值传递，也可以用于量词：This makes our logic a first-order logic. In a higher-order logic, predicates can be both passed as values and used as quantifiers:

Symmetric(P) = all x, y: P(x, y) == P(y, x)

多数数学家宁愿坚持使用一阶逻辑，因为高阶逻辑太“强大”了。正如我采访过的一位逻辑学家所说：“你可不想让你的逻辑突然造出一艘火箭。”这可以粗略类比计算机科学中的图灵完备性。分析图灵完备语言比分析限制更多的语言更困难。Most mathematicians prefer to stick with first-order logic because higher order logic is too “powerful”. As one logician I interviewed put it, “you don’t want your logic suddenly building a rocket ship.” A rough analogy would be to Turing completeness in computer science. It’s harder to analyze a Turing complete language than a more limited one.

[[应用：类型论，还有理论计算机科学，我想是的]][[Applications: type theory, theoretical computer science I think]]

构造性逻辑Constructive Logic

在本书最最开头，我说过“所有谓词都返回真或假”。这就是排中律：任何陈述不是真就是假。陈述不可能处于某种“第三种状态”。At the very very beginning of the book, I said “all predicates return true or false”. This is the Law of Excluded Middle: any statement is true or false. There is no “third thing” a statement can be.

这带来了一件不同寻常的事：如果要证明某件事为真，可以选择证明它“并非为假”。如果要证明一个集合非空，也可以改为证明这个集合不可能为空。这称为“非构造性证明”，因为你并没有真正构造出该集合中的一个值。This leads to something unusual: if you want to prove something true, you have the option of proving it “non-false”. And if you want to prove a set is nonempty, you can instead prove that it’s impossible for the set to be empty. This is called a “non-constructive proof”, since you aren’t actually constructing a value inside that set.

我最喜欢的例子是国际象棋。想象我们玩一个略有变化的版本：不是白方总是先走，而是可以选择先走还是后走。有了这条额外规则，就可以轻易证明，白方拥有一个万无一失、能始终获胜或和棋的策略：My favorite example of this is Chess. Imagine we are playing a slight variation where, instead of White always moving first, they can choose whether to move first or second. With this extra rule, we can trivially prove that White has a foolproof strategy to always win or tie:

假设白方没有万无一失的策略。那么，只要双方都完美行棋，黑方就总能获胜。但这时白方可以放弃第一回合，实际上成为后手，再遵循黑方的必胜策略。这意味着黑方没有必胜策略，也就意味着白方必定有一个万无一失的策略。Assume White doesn’t have a foolproof strategy. Then, assuming perfect play, Black always wins. But then White can pass on their first turn, making them effectively the second player, and then follow the winning strategy for Black. This means that Black doesn’t have a winning strategy, which means White must have a foolproof one.

这个证明优雅而严密。但对于那个万无一失的策略到底是什么，它没有提供任何信息，所以国际象棋仍然顽固地难以求解。It’s an elegant and watertight proof. It also gives us zero information on what the foolproof strategy actually is, and so chess remains stubbornly intractable.

非构造性证明让一些数学家感到不满，于是他们提出了另一种逻辑，称为构造性逻辑。构造性逻辑没有排中律，也没有双重否定规则：不能把 !!P 替换为 P。去掉这两条规则，使得编写证明和变换陈述更加困难。但作为回报，它保证要证明某个事物存在，唯一方式就是真正找出一个实例。Non-constructive proofs bother some mathematicians, who proposed an alternate form of logic called Constructive Logic. Constructive logic doesn’t have the law of excluded middle, nor does it have double-negation: you can’t replace !!P with P. These two removals mean that writing proofs and manipulating statements is harder. But in return, it guarantees the only way to prove the existence of something is to actually find an example.

构造性逻辑的另一个结果是，没有排中律，蕴含的行为就能更接近日常语言。“如果我叫 Greg，那么我就是英格兰国王”这个陈述在经典逻辑中在数学上为真（我不叫 Greg），但在日常生活中并不是一个真陈述。在构造性逻辑中，它也不一定为真。Another consequence of constructive logic is that without excluded middle, implication can work a little more like it does in normal language. The statement “if I was named Greg, then I’d be king of England” is mathematical true in classical logic (I’m not named Greg), but it’s not a true statement in day to day life. And it doesn’t have to be in constructive logic, either.

函数式编程风格的类型系统在本质上是构造性的。类型为 Int -> Bool 的函数是一个“证明”：如果整数存在，布尔值也存在，因为有一种方法能把一个整数实例转换成一个布尔值实例。Functional programming-style type systems are constructive by nature. A function of type Int -> Bool is a “proof” that if integers exist, booleans do too, because there’s a way to turn an example of an integer into an example of a boolean.

模态逻辑Modal Logic

谓词逻辑用关于数量的陈述扩展布尔值：陈述 P 是对集合中的所有元素为真，还是对至少一个元素为真？模态逻辑则用关于性质的陈述扩展布尔值：陈述 P 是“必然”为真，还是“可能”为真？Predicate logic augments booleans with statements over quantity: is statement P true for all elements of a set, or true for at least one? Modal logic instead augments booleans with statements of quality: is statement P true “necessarily”, or “possibly”?

例如，假设称量某个物体得到 100 克，但秤有 0.5 克的不确定误差。那么真实重量必然小于 101 克，并且可能小于 99.9 克。“必然”和“可能”互为对偶，因此“可能 P”等同于“并非必然非 P”。For example, say we weigh something and find it is 100 grams, but our scale has an uncertainty error of 0.5 grams. The true weight is necessarily less than 101 grams, and possibly less than 99.9 grams. Necessarily and possibly are duals, so “possibly P” is the same as “not necessarily not P”.

除此之外，“必然”和“可能”的含义并不明确，因此也就存在许多不同的模态逻辑。哲学家用模态逻辑探索知识、道德、不确定性以及其他许多事物的本质。Beyond that, what “necessarily” and “possibly” mean are vague, which in turn means that there’s many different modal logics. Philosophers use modal logic to explore the nature of knowledge, morality, uncertainty, and many other things.

但最重要的模态逻辑，你已经见过了：时间模态。TLA+ 的始终和最终，其实就是“必然”和“可能”！But the most important modal logic is one you’ve already seen: the mode of time. TLA+’s’s always and eventually is just “necessarily” and “possibly”!

模态与量词（all 和 some）相互独立：你可以只有模态、只有量词，也可以两者都有。Modes are independent of quantifiers (all and some): you can have modes, quantifiers, or both.

在 all x in set: P(x) => Q(x) 中，我们只对同时满足 P(x) 的元素检查 Q(x)。在 all x in {x \in set: P(x)}: Q(x) 中，我们筛掉所有不满足 P(x) 的元素，然后对剩余元素检查 Q(x)。等价性由此得出。In all x in set: P(x) => Q(x) we only check Q(x) on the elements that also satisfy P(x). In all x in {x \in set: P(x)}: Q(x) we filter out all of the elements that don’t satisfy P(x) and then check Q(x) on the rest. Equivalence follows.

另一方面，max_avail_price 的后置条件变得更复杂了。如果返回值是数值，它仍然是可用商品的最高价格。如果返回值是 None，则表示没有可用商品。因此，新契约如下：On the other hand, max_avail_price’s postconditions get more complicated. If the return value is a number, it still is the highest price of an available item. If the return value is None, then there were no available items. So the new contract is this:

ensures:

  o != None =>

      some i in available:
        1. i.price = out
        2. all i2 in available: i2.price <= i.price

首先，如果 S 有 s 个元素，T 有 t 个元素，那么 #S * #T == s*t。由于集合的基数不取决于它有哪些具体元素，只取决于元素数量，因此可以放心地假设 S = 1..=s 且 T = 1..=t。现在，只需证明 (1..=s) x (1..=t) 有 s*t 个元素。为此，我把所有元素排成一个网格：First of all, if S has s elements and T has t elements, #S * #T == s*t. Since the cardinality of the set does not depend on what elements it has, only the number of elements, I can safely assume that S = 1..=s and T = 1..=t. Now, I just need to show that (1..=s) x (1..=t) has s*t elements. To do this, I will put all of the elements in a grid:

(1, 1) (1, 2)  ... (1, t)
(2, 1) (2, 2)  ... (2, t)
   .      .     .    .
(s, 1) (s, 2)  ... (s, t)

这个网格有 s 行、t 列，因此有 s*t 个元素。This grid has s rows and t columns, so it has s*t elements.

可以把 Transfer(t) 重命名为 TransferAliceToBob(t)，将反方向的转账写成一个新谓词，再把它加入 next。We can rename Transfer(t) to TransferAliceToBob(t), write the converse as a new predicate, and then add it to next.

TransferBobToAlice(t: Time) =
  some value in 1..=bob[t]:
    1. alice[t+1] == alice[t] - value
    2. bob[t+1] == bob[t] + value

Next(t) =
  || TransferAliceToBob(t)
  || TransferBobToAlice(t)

那么，Alice 和 Bob 能在同一个步骤中相互转账吗？不能。假设双方开始时各有 10 美元，都试图向对方转账五美元。由 TransferAliceToBob 可得：Now, can Alice and Bob transfer to each other in the same step? No. Let’s say they both start with 10 dollars and each try to transfer five dollars to each other. By TransferAliceToBob we have:

1. alice[1] == alice[0] - 5 == 5
2. bob[1] == bob[0] + 5 == 15

而由 TransferBobToAlice 可得：And by TransferBobToAlice, we have:

1. bob[1] == bob[0] - 5 == 5
2. alice[1] == alice[0] + 5 == 15

这样就得到了 alice[1] == 5 && alice[1] == 15，它始终为假。So now we have alice[1] == 5 && alice[1] == 15, which is always false.

  1. “T 与 P 和 R 一样强”就是 T => P && R。由于 P => Q，因此也有 T => Q，意味着 T 与 Q 一样强。“T is as strong as P and R” is T => P && R. Since P => Q, T => Q too, meaning T is as strong as Q.

test false 会拒绝 max 的任何有缺陷的实现……但它也会拒绝正确实现！一个测试之所以是“max 的测试”，就在于正确实现能够通过它。这意味着 false 根本不是 max 的测试（也不可能比它们更强）。test false will reject any buggy implementation of max… but it will also reject a correct implementation! What makes a given test “a test of max” is that it will pass for a correct implementation, meaning false isn’t a test of max at all (and cannot be stronger than them).

相比之下，test true 确实是 max 的有效测试，而且实际上是最弱的测试。By contrast, test true is a valid test of max, and in fact the weakest possible test.

数据库约束Database Constraints

数据库原生就能表示一些约束，例如 NOT NULL、UNIQUE 和外键约束。但有些更强大的约束，数据库可能无法表示。即便如此，能够表达这些约束，也能让我们更容易找到其他强制实施它们的方法，因此这些复杂约束十分有用。不过，首先需要把它们表示出来，而这就需要逻辑。Databases can natively represent some constraints, like NOT NULL, UNIQUE, and foreign key constraints. But there are more powerful constraints databases may not be able to represent. Even so, being able to express them makes it easier for us to find other ways of enforcing them, making these complex constraints quite useful. First, though, we need to represent them, and that requires logic.

逻辑Logic

一种记录语法A Record Syntax

首先，假设所有数据库表都表示集合。如果有一个名为 Users 的表，那么表中的每条记录就表示集合 Users 中的一个元素。每个用户都有一个唯一的整数“id”。能否纯粹用谓词做到这一点？Let’s start by assuming that all database tables represent sets. If we have a table called Users then each record in that table represents an element from the set Users. Each user has a unique integer “id”. Can we do that purely with predicates?

UserId(u: User, id: Int) = `user u has id `id``

EwEwEw =
  all u in Users:
    some id in Int:
      1. UserId(u, id)
      2. all notid in Int - {id}:
         !UserId(u, notid)

好吧，这太糟糕了。显然，我们需要一种表示记录的方式，不必为“用户有 id”写上六行。如前所述，如果某件事谈起来很笨拙，就创造新的记法来讨论它。因此，让我们引入一种记录语法：Okay that sucks, clearly we’re going to want a way to represent records without having to write six lines for “users have ids.” As mentioned before, if something is clunky to talk about, we come up with new notation to discuss it. So let’s introduce a record syntax:

record Users {
  id: Int
}

把它理解为“每个用户恰好有一个 id，该 id 属于整数集合”。如果想表示可空列，可以用集合的并来实现。为方便起见，规定 set + x 与 set | {x} 是同一种写法。Take this to mean “every user has exactly one id, which is in the set of Integers.” If we wanted to represent a nullable column, we could do that with a set union. We’ll say that set + x is the same as writing set | {x} for convenience.

record Users {
  id: Int
  email: String + NULL
}

简单约束Simple Constraints

我们的记录记法可以表示 SQL 约束 NOT NULL，但还不能表示约束 UNIQUE。虽然可以扩展语法来涵盖它，但这是一本关于逻辑的书，所以我们来寻找逻辑上的解决方案。Our record notation can represent the SQL constraint NOT NULL, but it can’t yet represent the constraint UNIQUE. While we could extend our syntax to cover this, this is a book about logic, so let’s look for a logical solution.

constraint UserIdUnique = `no two users have the same id`

我在前面加上“constraint”，因为我个人喜欢使用大量辅助谓词，希望显式标出哪些才是真正的系统约束。无论如何，这是一个标准的唯一性谓词（使用 disj）：I put “constraint” in front because I personally like using a lot of helper predicates, and I want to explicitly label the ones that are actual system constraints. Anyway, this is a standard uniqueness predicate (using disj):

constraint UserIdUnique =
  all disj u1, u2 in Users:
    u1.id != u2.id

这个约束有趣的地方在于，它约束的不是单个用户，而是用户对。每个用户单独看都是有效记录，但两者放在一起就违反了约束。Something interesting about this constraint is that it’s not a constraint on individual users, it’s a constraint on pairs of users. Each user is a valid record on its own, but both of them together violates our constraint.

练习：复合键Exercise: Compound keys

给定Given

record Books {
  title: str,
  author: str
}

constraint UniqueCompound =
  `title + author is a compound unique key`

两本书可以同名，也可以有同一位作者，但不能同时拥有相同的书名和作者组合。请写出谓词 UniqueCompound。Two books can have the same title and two books can have the same author, but two books cannot have the same title/author combo. Write the predicate UniqueCompound.

解答Solution

外键约束Foreign Key Constraints

我们来做一件稍复杂的事。假设还有一张 Groups 表，并且所有群组都必须有一个用户担任管理员。在 SQL 中，大致会是这样：Let’s do something a little more complicated. Say we also have a Groups table, and all groups must have an admin user. In SQL, that would look something like:

CREATE TABLE group (
    id integer,
    admin_id REFERENCES user(id)
    // ...
);

下面是直译成“记录语法”的结果：Here’s the literal translation to “record syntax”:

record Groups {
  id: Int
  admin_id: Int
}

我们可以这样把外键约束表示为逻辑谓词：Here’s how we can represent the foreign key constraint as a logical predicate:

IsAdmin(u, g) = u.id = g.admin_id

constraint AllGroupsHaveAdmin =
  all g in Groups:
    some u in Users:
      IsAdmin(u, g)

注意这里的“交替量词”：我们把 some 嵌套在 all 内。这表示“对所有群组，都存在某个用户担任管理员”。不过，每个群组对应的用户可以不同。如果改写成Notice the “alternating quantifiers”: we’re nesting a some inside of an all. This says “for all groups, there is some user who is the Admin”. It can be a different user per group, though. If we instead wrote

"constraint" AllGroupsHaveAdmin =
  some u in Users:
    all g in Groups:
      IsAdmin(u, g)

那就变成了“存在某个用户，是所有群组的管理员”。That would instead say “there is some user who is the admin of all groups.”

练习：空外键Exercise: Null foreign keys

有时，外键列可以为 null：Sometimes a foreign key column can be null:

record Groups {
  id: Int
  admin_id: Int + NULL
}

但如果不为 null，它就必须指向一个用户。请对此建模。If it’s not null, though, it must point to a user. Model this.

解答Solution

或者，也可以用如下这种不太严谨的方式（使用集合映射记法）：Alternatively, we could do something handwavey like this (using set map notation):

record Groups {
  id: Int
  admin_id: {u.id for u in Users}
}

可以用同样的方式加入多对多关联表。让我们加入群组成员关系：We can use the same thing to add many to many tables. Let’s add group memberships:

record GroupMembership {
  id: int
  user_id: int
  group_id: int
}

MemberOf(u, g) =
  some gm in GroupMemberships:
    1. gm.user_id = u.id
    2. gm.group_id = g.id

练习Exercise

写出约束：“两条不同的群组成员记录不能同时对应同一个用户和同一个群组。”Write the constraint “two different group memberships can’t be for the same user and the same group.”

解答Solution

写出约束：“群组的管理员必须是该群组的成员。”Write the constraint “The admin of a group must be a member of that group.”

令 #S 表示 S 中的元素个数。写出约束：“所有群组都至多只能有五个成员。”Let #S be the number of elements in S. Write the constraint “all groups can only have five members at most.”

更复杂的约束More Complex Constraints

既然已经跨过了表示基本 SQL 结构的初步障碍，我们就可以充分运用逻辑的力量来表达约束。这远远超出了专用 SQL 关键字所能做到的范围。例如，用逻辑很容易表达“每个群组都需要一位是活跃用户的管理员”：Now that we’re past the basic hurdles of representing basic SQL constructs, we can use the full power of logic to express our constraints. This can go far beyond what we can do with the dedicated SQL keywords. For example, it’s easy to use logic to say “every group needs an admin that’s an active user”:

constraint AllGroupsHaveAdmin =
  all g in Groups:
    some u in Users:
      1. IsAdmin(g, u)
      2. IsActive(u)

或者，所有在某个日期之后创建的群组都需要一位活跃的管理员：Or all groups created after a certain date need an active admin:

constraint all g in Groups:
  g.date > legacy_date =>
    some u in Users:
        1. IsAdmin(g, u)
        2. IsActive(u)

而这还只是一个基本数据库约束的两种变体！只要你能想到某个约束，很可能就有某个产品需要它。And that’s just a couple variants on a fundamental database constraint! If you can think of a constraint, there’s probably some product out there that needs it.

[[使用逻辑的意义就在于能够思考这些问题。如果只考虑那些可以用 SQL 原生表达的约束，就无法识别出许多你可能需要的约束类别。]][[The point of using logic is being able to think about these things. If you restrict yourself to only thinking of constraints that you can express natively in SQL, you won’t recognize large classes of constraints that you may need.]]

注Note

这里还需要写些什么才有用？只加例子？还是介绍约束的类别？What else needs to be written here to make this useful? Just examples? Classes of constraints?

变更约束Change Constraints

有时，约束针对的不是记录是什么，而是记录可以如何变化。例如，可以规定群组在开始时没有管理员：Sometimes a constraint isn’t on what record is but on how a record could change. For example, we might have that groups can start without an admin:

record Groups {
  id: Int
  admin_id: Int + NULL
}

但群组一旦有了管理员，就不能再回到没有管理员的状态。But once a group has an admin, it cannot go back to having no admin.

为此建模时，可以借用前面处理决策表时的一个技巧：每当 x 发生变化，就定义 x 为（该瞬间的）旧值，x'（读作 x 撇）为（该瞬间的）新值。To model this, we can adapt a trick we used earlier with decision tables: whenever x changes, we can define x to be the old value (in that instant) and x' (x-prime) to be the new value (in that instant).

constraint NoNullAfterAdmin =
  all g in Groups:
    g.admin_id != NULL => g.admin_id' != NULL

因此，一旦 admin_id 不为 null，下一个值也不能为 null，意味着它再也不能变回 null。So once the admin_id isn’t null, the next value can’t be null either, meaning that it can never go back to null.

这也适用于状态机列：一条记录可以经历 WAITING -> READY 或 READY -> DONE，但不能经历 WAITING -> DONE。这种情况下，通常应该“允许 x 变成它自身”：This is also useful for state machine columns: a record can go WAITING -> READY or READY -> DONE, but not WAITING -> DONE. In that case it’s considered good form to “allow x to change to itself”:

constraint StateMachineTransitions ==
  all t in Tasks:
    1. t.status = "WAITING" => t.status' in {"WAITING", "READY"}
    2. t.status = "READY => t.status' in {"READY", "DONE"}

练习：转移辅助谓词Exercise: Transition Helper

编写一个辅助谓词 ValidTransitions(task, from, to)，使我们能够这样写出 StateMachineTransitions 的主体：Write a helper predicate ValidTransitions(task, from, to), so that we can write the body of StateMachineTransitions this way:

all t in Tasks:
  1. ValidTransitions(task, "WAITING", {"READY"})
  2. ValidTransitions(task, "READY", {"DONE"})

注意，to 将是一个转移的集合。Note that to is going to be a set of transitions.

解答Solution

实践：强制实施数据库约束In Practice: Enforcing Database Constraints

现在，理论要落到实践中了。一旦知道有哪些约束，该如何确保系统能够强制实施它们？This is where the theory becomes practice. Once you know what the constraints are, how do you make sure your system can enforce them?

盘点你具备的能力Take stock of your capabilities

你的系统有哪些组件，它们能强制实施什么？What are the components of your system, and what can they enforce?

例如，如果使用 Postgres，就可以建立行级约束 [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html]：For example, if you’re working with Postgres, you can make row-level constraints [https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html]:

CREATE TABLE intervals (
    id integer,
    start integer,
    end integer
    CHECK (start < end)
);

如果使用 Ruby on Rails [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_record_validations.html] 这样的 Web 框架，就有可定制的验证代码。组件能直接强制实施的要求更容易处理，在实施过程中也更不容易出错。If you’re using a web framework like Ruby on Rails [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_record_validations.html], you have customizable validation code. Things that the components can directly enforce are easier to handle, and you’re less likely to make a mistake enforcing them.

要注意，多数人对工具的使用远未达到专家水平。我直到写这本书时，才知道 Postgres 能（通过 TRIGGER）检查变更约束。Be aware that most of us don’t using our tools at anywhere near the expert level. I didn’t know until writing book that Postgres can check change constraints (via TRIGGER).

按可实施性寻找类别Look for categories of enforceability

对于特定工具，某些类别的约束相对更容易或更难强制实施。多数数据库非常擅长强制实施“这一列必须唯一”和“这一列除了 null 值之外必须唯一”。但对于“这一列除了数值 19 之外必须唯一”这样的要求，就没那么擅长了。Certain classes of constraints are relatively easier or harder to enforce with respect to certain tooling. Most database are very good at enforcing “this column must unique” and “this column must be unique except for null values”. But they’re worse at enforcing something like “this column must be unique except for the number 19”.

有些限制可以绕过。SQL 没有蕴含运算符，所以不能写约束 P => Q。但可以写 NOT P OR Q。Some limitations can be worked around. SQL doesn’t have an implication operator, so you can’t write the constraint P => Q. But you can write NOT P OR Q.

尽早实施，也在最后把关Enforce early, enforce late

设想服务器接收到一条新记录，并尝试将其写入数据库。是应该在服务器收到请求时尽早强制实施约束，还是在数据库真正尝试写入时尽晚强制实施？Consider a server receiving a new record, which it tries to write to the database. Is it better to enforce the constraint as early as possible when the server receives the request, or as late as possible when the database actually tries to write it?

两者各有好处。在服务器层实施约束，能尽早发现问题，从而改善用户体验。另一方面，它的稳健性较差。可能出现这样的竞态条件：两台服务器在任何一台写入记录之前，都验证了记录的唯一性，最终导致重复记录。如果在数据库层实施约束，这种情况就不可能发生。They both have their benefits. Enforcing it at the server level recognizes the problem as soon as possible, which can lead to a better user experience. On the other hand, it’s less robust. You can have a race condition where two servers both validate a record is unique before either writes the record, leading to duplicate records. This is impossible if you enforce the constraint at the database level.

因此，很有理由在早期和晚期都实施约束。这也有一个缺点：如果需要验证的约束发生变化，两处的实现可能会不同步。That’s a good reason to enforce both early and late. This also has a drawback: if the constraints you need to validate change, the two can get out of sync.

无法强制实施时，就转而检查If you can’t enforce, look instead

显然，最好从一开始就不发生违规。但有时工具无法防止约束被破坏，有时约束又超出我们的控制范围。你可能有这样一条约束：“所有外部链接都指向有效的网站”：It’s obviously better to never have a violation in the first place. But sometimes our tools aren’t capable of preventing broken constraints, and sometimes constraints are out of our control. You might have the constraint “all outgoing links are to valid websites”:

all l in Link:
  Resolves(l.url)

如果网站后来下线，即使系统中什么也没变，约束也被破坏了！因此，我们无法保证它始终成立。If the website goes down later, then the constraint is broken, even if nothing changed in your system! So that’s something we can’t guarantee always holds.

在这种情况下，我觉得写一个检查约束违规的脚本很方便。大致如下：In these cases, I find it handy to write a script that checks for broken constraints. Something like this:

for l in SELECT * FROM links:
  if get(l.url).response != 200:
     register_as_broken(l)

编程语言通常比约束语言灵活得多，因此更容易用它们编码约束。脚本可能只需每晚运行一次，并在早晨向你发送报告。Programming languages are typically much more flexible than constraint languages, so it’s easier to encode constraints in them. A script might only need to run nightly and can send you a report in the morning.

当约束相对不那么重要时，这种技巧更有用，所以首先了解相关风险很有帮助。This technique is more useful when the constraint is relatively minor, which is why it’s useful to understand the risks involved first.

小结Summary

  1. 数据库约束实际上就是作为性质的逻辑谓词。Database constraints are actually logical predicates as properties.

  2. 外键约束也是如此。So are foreign key constraints.

  3. 谓词逻辑能够表达的约束种类远比数据库多。Predicate logic can express a much wider variety of constraints than databases can.

  4. 能表达的约束越多，就越能找到办法实施更多约束，无论是在数据库中还是在别处。The more constraints you can express, the more constraints you can find ways to enforce, whether with the database or somewhere else.

到目前为止，我们的逻辑始终紧贴数据库：我们讨论的是数据库表和记录的性质。[[但数据库只是数据模型的一种不完美实现，而数据模型是我们试图使之清晰可理解的那部分世界的概念化表示。]] 下一章，我们将上升一个抽象层次，用逻辑研究数据模型。So far we’ve been keeping the logic very close to the database: we’re talking about properties of database tables and records. [[But the database is just an imperfect implementation of the data model, the conceptual slice of the world we’re trying to make legible.]] Next chapter we will use logic to study our data model, one level of abstraction higher.
